The operation will fail with appropriate error messages if the SKU has any active dependencies. Sellers should ensure that the SKU has no active inventory, orders, or cart references before attempting deletion.

Common use cases include removing discontinued product variants, cleaning up test SKUs created during product setup, or eliminating variants that were created in error. Before deletion, sellers should consider whether archiving or marking the SKU as unavailable would be more appropriate for maintaining historical records.

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a paginated list of historical snapshots for a specific product sale. It operates on the shopping_mall_sale_snapshots table, which captures point-in-time records of sale information for audit trails and version control. Snapshots allow tracking of how sale details (pricing, descriptions, specifications) have changed over time, providing transparency and accountability in the marketplace.
operations.summary: Retrieve paginated historical snapshots of a product sale
operations.description:
Fetch a filtered and paginated list of historical point-in-time snapshots for a specific product sale listing.

This operation provides access to the complete audit trail of a product sale's historical states. Each snapshot represents a frozen record of the sale's information at a specific moment in time, capturing changes to pricing, product descriptions, images, variants, and other sale attributes. This functionality is essential for transparency, dispute resolution, regulatory compliance, and understanding the evolution of product listings over time.

The operation supports advanced filtering and pagination to efficiently navigate through potentially large snapshot histories. Users can search snapshots by creation date ranges, sort chronologically to see the progression of changes, and paginate through results to manage large datasets. This is particularly valuable for sales that have undergone numerous modifications, allowing stakeholders to trace exactly when and how product information changed.

Security and access control: Snapshot visibility depends on user authorization. Sellers can view snapshots of their own products to review their listing history. Admins have broader access for marketplace oversight, fraud detection, and dispute resolution. Buyers may have limited access to snapshots related to their purchases for verification purposes. The operation enforces these access controls based on the authenticated user's role and relationship to the sale.

Business applications include: tracking price changes for competitive analysis, verifying product descriptions at the time of purchase for customer service, investigating seller behavior patterns for fraud detection, providing evidence in dispute resolution, and maintaining regulatory compliance for marketplace operations. The snapshot system ensures that historical product information is immutable and trustworthy.

This operation integrates with the shopping_mall_sale_snapshots table as defined in the Prisma schema, which has a snapshot stance indicating it contains historical audit trail data. Related operations include retrieving individual snapshot details (GET) and the main sale listing operations that trigger snapshot creation.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific point-in-time snapshot of a product sale's historical information from the shopping_mall_sale_snapshots table. This operation provides access to complete product state as it existed at a specific moment, preserving historical accuracy for audit trails, compliance reporting, and dispute resolution.

Snapshots are append-only historical records created when significant product changes occur, enabling tracking of price changes, description modifications, and product evolution over time. Each snapshot denormalizes complete product information including title, description, pricing details, variant configurations, category assignment, and seller information as they existed at the snapshot creation time.

This endpoint requires authentication to ensure proper access control to historical product data. The operation validates that the requested snapshot belongs to the specified sale by matching both the sale code and snapshot ID. Historical snapshots are particularly valuable for order verification, ensuring that orders reference accurate product information as it appeared at purchase time.

The response includes all denormalized fields from the snapshot record: product code, title, description, brand, condition, status, dimensions, weight, return policy, warranty information, and timestamps. This complete historical view supports compliance requirements and provides sellers with product evolution tracking capabilities.

Related operations: GET /sales/{saleCode} retrieves current product information, while this endpoint specifically accesses historical snapshot data for audit and verification purposes.

operations.specification: This operation retrieves the current inventory stock information for a specific product SKU variant. It operates on the shopping_mall_inventory_stocks table, which maintains real-time available quantities for each product variant. The operation requires the SKU ID to locate the corresponding inventory record and returns current stock levels including total quantity, reserved quantity, available quantity, and low stock threshold settings. This endpoint supports inventory monitoring, stock validation during checkout, and seller inventory management workflows.
operations.summary: Retrieve current inventory stock levels for a product SKU variant
operations.description:
Retrieve the current inventory stock information for a specific product SKU variant from the shopping_mall_inventory_stocks table. This operation provides real-time visibility into stock levels, availability status, and inventory thresholds for a single product variant.

The inventory stock record represents the single source of truth for how many units of a specific SKU are currently available for purchase. The response includes total quantity (complete stock level), reserved quantity (units temporarily held during checkout), and available quantity (calculated as total minus reserved, representing units buyers can immediately purchase).

This endpoint is critical for several workflows: buyers checking product availability before purchase, sellers monitoring inventory levels across their catalog, and the checkout system validating stock availability during order placement. The low stock threshold field indicates the seller-configured level that triggers restock alerts.

Stock quantities are maintained through inventory transactions including sales, returns, restocks, and manual adjustments. Reserved quantities represent units in pending checkouts that are temporarily allocated but not yet confirmed as sold. When available quantity reaches zero, the SKU becomes unavailable for purchase until restocked.

The operation supports both seller self-service inventory monitoring (sellers viewing their own SKU stock levels) and administrative oversight (admins monitoring platform-wide inventory). Accurate real-time inventory data prevents overselling and ensures buyers see correct availability information.

Related operations: PATCH /inventoryStocks searches across multiple SKUs for bulk inventory monitoring, while this endpoint provides detailed stock information for a single SKU variant.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the product SKU variant

responseBody.description: Current inventory stock levels and threshold configuration for the SKU

Retrieve a comprehensive list of inventory transaction records with advanced filtering and pagination capabilities. This operation provides detailed audit trail access for all inventory movements across the shopping mall platform.

The inventory transactions table serves as a complete historical ledger of all stock changes, capturing every addition, removal, reservation, and release of inventory. Each transaction record includes the associated SKU, transaction type, quantity change, timestamp, and optional reference information linking to orders or other business events that triggered the inventory movement.

This operation supports filtering by multiple criteria including specific SKUs, transaction types (such as 'purchase', 'sale', 'adjustment', 'reservation', 'release'), date ranges for when transactions occurred, and sorting by timestamp or quantity. The response includes pagination to handle large transaction histories efficiently, with configurable page sizes and cursor-based navigation for optimal performance.

The operation integrates with the shopping_mall_inventory_transactions table as defined in the Prisma schema, which maintains a complete snapshot-based audit trail of all inventory changes. Transaction records are immutable once created, ensuring data integrity for compliance and auditing purposes.

operations.summary: Update an existing inventory reservation record
operations.description:
Update the details of an existing inventory reservation in the system. This operation allows modification of reservation parameters including reserved quantity, expiration timestamp, and reservation status.

Inventory reservations can be updated for several business scenarios: extending the reservation period when a buyer needs more time to complete checkout, adjusting the reserved quantity if the buyer modifies their cart before completing purchase, or releasing a reservation early if the buyer abandons the checkout process.

The update operation validates that the new reservation parameters are valid, such as ensuring the requested quantity doesn't exceed available inventory when increasing a reservation, or that expiration times are set to future timestamps. The system prevents updates that would violate inventory constraints or business rules.

Security and authorization: Only authorized actors can update reservations. Typically, the system automatically manages reservation updates during the checkout flow, but admins may have manual override capabilities for special cases or issue resolution. Buyers cannot directly modify reservations - updates occur through cart and checkout operations.

This operation integrates with the shopping_mall_inventory_reservations table as defined in the Prisma schema, ensuring all updates maintain referential integrity with related SKU and order records.

operations.specification: This operation deletes an inventory reservation record from the shopping_mall_inventory_reservations table. Inventory reservations are temporary holds placed on product SKU quantities during the checkout process to prevent overselling. This operation is used to release a reservation when it's no longer needed, such as when a checkout is abandoned, a cart item is removed, or an order is successfully completed and the reservation should be converted to actual inventory deduction.
operations.summary: Delete an inventory reservation to release temporarily held stock
operations.description:
Delete an inventory reservation record to release the temporarily held stock quantity back to available inventory. This operation is used when a reservation is no longer needed and should be cancelled.

Inventory reservations are created during the checkout process to temporarily hold product quantities and prevent overselling while a buyer completes their purchase. Each reservation has an expiration time, after which it becomes invalid. This operation allows for manual cancellation of reservations before their natural expiration.

Common use cases include: (1) When a buyer removes items from their cart before checkout completion, (2) When a checkout session is abandoned and needs cleanup, (3) When an order is successfully placed and the reservation should be released as inventory is deducted through the order fulfillment process, (4) When system cleanup processes remove expired or orphaned reservations.

Security considerations: The operation validates that the reservation exists and is in a valid state for deletion. The system ensures that releasing the reservation properly updates the corresponding inventory stock levels. After deletion, the reserved quantity becomes available again for other buyers to purchase.

This operation integrates with the shopping_mall_inventory_reservations table from the Prisma schema. The deletion is permanent and cannot be undone. If the reservation has already been consumed by order placement, the operation may fail or have no effect depending on business rules.

The operation supports advanced query parameters for filtering by product attributes, price ranges, availability status, and sorting options.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve the authenticated buyer's shopping cart items with filtering
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of shopping cart items for the currently authenticated buyer. This operation provides the buyer's personal cart contents with support for complex queries including product filtering, sorting, and pagination.

The shopping cart is a buyer-specific collection of products they intend to purchase. Each cart item references a specific product SKU (variant) with a desired quantity. The cart persists across sessions, allowing buyers to save items for later purchase. This operation returns the current state of the buyer's cart with full product details for each item.

The operation supports comprehensive filtering and search capabilities including: filtering by product category, price range filtering, availability status filtering (in-stock vs out-of-stock items), sorting by date added, price, or product name, and pagination for large carts. The response includes detailed information about each cart item including the product details, selected SKU variant, current price, availability status, and quantity.

Security considerations: This operation is restricted to authenticated buyers and only returns cart items belonging to the current user based on their JWT token. Buyers cannot access other users' carts. The operation performs real-time validation of item availability and pricing, alerting buyers to any changes since items were added.

Business rules: Cart items may reference products that are no longer available or have changed in price. The response indicates such discrepancies so the buyer can make informed decisions. Quantity limits per item may apply based on available inventory. Items in the cart do not create inventory reservations until the buyer begins checkout.

This operation integrates with the shopping_mall_cart_items table and related product, SKU, and inventory tables from the Prisma schema. It provides essential functionality for the shopping experience, allowing buyers to review and manage their intended purchases before proceeding to checkout.

operations.summary: Remove a specific item from the buyer's shopping cart
operations.description:
Remove a specific product item from the authenticated buyer's shopping cart. This operation allows buyers to delete items they no longer wish to purchase without affecting other items in their cart.

The operation verifies ownership before deletion to ensure security. The buyer's identity is automatically extracted from the JWT authentication token, and the system confirms that the cart item with the specified cartItemId belongs to the authenticated buyer. If the cart item doesn't exist or belongs to a different buyer, the operation returns an appropriate error.

Security considerations include authentication requirement and ownership validation. Only the cart owner can delete their cart items, preventing unauthorized modifications to other users' shopping carts. The operation is idempotent - attempting to delete an already-deleted or non-existent cart item returns a success response.

When a cart item is removed, any associated inventory reservations are released, making the stock available for other buyers. The operation completes immediately and does not return the deleted cart item data.

Related operations include updating cart item quantity (PUT /buyers/me/cart/items/{cartItemId}), retrieving the full cart (PATCH /buyers/me/cart/items), and adding items to cart (POST /buyers/me/cart/items). Buyers may also move items to their wishlist before deletion using the wishlist operations.

operations.description:
Move a specific product from the authenticated buyer's wishlist to their shopping cart for immediate purchase preparation.

This operation transfers a wishlist item to the cart by removing it from the wishlist and creating a corresponding cart entry with the buyer's specified quantity. Since wishlist items represent passive interest without quantities, the buyer must provide the desired purchase quantity during the move operation. The operation validates the requested quantity against current inventory availability to prevent overselling.

The product's current price is captured as the unit_price_snapshot in the newly created cart item, which may differ from the price_snapshot stored in the original wishlist item if prices changed since the item was wishlisted. This enables price change detection and buyer notification during cart viewing.

The wishlist item is soft-deleted (deleted_at timestamp set) rather than hard-deleted, supporting potential undo functionality within the 10-second recovery window. The cart item is created with the same SKU variant (preserving selected color, size, and options) from the wishlist item.

This operation requires buyer authentication and validates that the wishlist item belongs to the authenticated buyer before performing the move. Cart synchronization across devices occurs within 5 seconds for authenticated buyers.

operations.summary: Search and retrieve a filtered, paginated list of orders

Retrieve a comprehensive, filtered, and paginated list of orders from the marketplace. This operation provides advanced search capabilities for finding orders based on multiple criteria including order number, status, creation date ranges, buyer information, seller information, payment status, shipping status, and order total amounts.

The operation supports role-based data filtering to ensure users only see orders they are authorized to access. Buyers see only their own orders, sellers see orders containing items they are selling, and administrators have access to all orders across the platform. The filtering logic is automatically applied based on the authenticated user's actor type extracted from the JWT token.

The response includes order summary information optimized for list displays, with options to include related data such as order items, seller information, and shipping details based on the actor's authorization level.

Security considerations include rate limiting for search operations to prevent abuse, and appropriate filtering of sensitive order information based on the requesting user's authorization level. Personal information and payment details are masked or excluded for users without proper permissions.

operations.specification: This operation creates a new order in the shopping marketplace by processing items from the buyer's shopping cart and initiating the checkout workflow. It operates on the shopping_mall_orders table and creates associated records in shopping_mall_order_sellers, shopping_mall_order_items, shopping_mall_inventory_reservations, and shopping_mall_payment_transactions tables. This endpoint handles the critical business transaction of converting cart items into confirmed orders with payment processing, inventory reservation, and multi-seller order splitting when necessary.
operations.summary: Create a new order from shopping cart items with payment processing
operations.description:
Create a new order by processing selected items from the authenticated buyer's shopping cart, validating inventory availability, calculating totals, processing payment, and reserving inventory for fulfillment. This operation executes the complete checkout workflow that transforms cart items into a confirmed purchase order.

The operation validates that all cart items are available and in stock, calculates order totals including product prices, quantities, taxes, shipping costs, and platform fees. It processes payment through the specified payment method, creates inventory reservations to prevent overselling, and splits the order into seller-specific portions when items come from multiple sellers. Each seller receives their portion of the order for independent fulfillment.

Security considerations include authentication to identify the buyer, validation of payment method ownership, verification of shipping address ownership, and prevention of race conditions during inventory reservation. The operation enforces business rules such as minimum order amounts, seller-specific shipping policies, and payment processing requirements.

This operation integrates with multiple Prisma schema tables including shopping_mall_orders (parent order), shopping_mall_order_sellers (seller-specific portions), shopping_mall_order_items (line items), shopping_mall_inventory_reservations (stock holds), shopping_mall_payment_transactions (payment records), and shopping_mall_cart_items (source items that are cleared after successful order creation). The response includes the complete created order with all nested relationships, payment confirmation, and order tracking information.

Related operations: Buyers must first add items to cart (POST /cart-items), manage shipping addresses (POST /buyer-addresses), and configure payment methods (POST /payment-methods) before creating orders. After order creation, buyers track orders (GET /orders/{orderId}) and sellers fulfill orders (PUT /order-sellers/{orderSellerId}).

responseBody.description: Complete created order information including order ID, payment confirmation, and initial order status

Orders that are in processing, shipped, or delivered states generally cannot be deleted and should use the cancellation workflow instead through the dedicated cancellation operations.

Security validation ensures that only authorized users can delete orders - buyers can only delete their own orders in eligible states. The operation validates order ownership, current status eligibility, and performs the soft deletion by setting the deleted_at field in the shopping_mall_orders table.

Submit a report against a product review that violates platform policies such as spam, offensive content, fake reviews, or other policy violations. This operation allows authenticated buyers to flag problematic reviews for moderator review.

The reporting system helps maintain review quality and authenticity by enabling the community to identify policy violations. Each report includes a reason category (from predefined options like 'spam', 'offensive', 'fake', 'irrelevant') and an optional detailed description explaining the concern.

Security: Only authenticated buyers can submit reports. The buyer_id is automatically extracted from the JWT authentication token. Duplicate reports from the same buyer for the same review may be prevented based on business rules. Rate limiting applies to prevent abuse.

The created report enters a pending moderation queue where admins can review and take appropriate action. Related operations include viewing report details (GET /reviews/{reviewId}/reports/{reportId}) and admin moderation workflows.

The response includes comprehensive report information such as the reason category (spam, offensive, fake, irrelevant, etc.), the optional detailed description provided by the reporter, the buyer who submitted the report, when the report was created, and any moderation actions taken.

Security: Access control depends on the requesting user. Admins can view all reports for moderation purposes. Buyers may only view their own submitted reports. The operation validates that the report belongs to the specified review and enforces appropriate authorization rules.

This operation is commonly used in admin moderation dashboards to review flagged content and make decisions about review visibility or user actions. It may also be used by buyers to check the status of reports they submitted.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves a paginated list of product reviews for a specific seller's products. It operates on the shopping_mall_reviews table, filtering reviews to show only those associated with products (sales) belonging to the specified seller.

IMPORTANT RELATIONSHIP PATH: The shopping_mall_reviews table does NOT have a direct foreign key to shopping_mall_sellers. To filter by seller, the query must traverse the relationship path: shopping_mall_reviews → shopping_mall_sales (via shopping_mall_sale_id) → shopping_mall_sellers (via shopping_mall_seller_id). This requires a JOIN operation in the implementation.

The operation supports comprehensive search capabilities including filtering by rating, verified purchase status, review date ranges, and sorting options. The seller filter is implemented by joining with the shopping_mall_sales table and matching the seller_id field.
operations.summary: Retrieve paginated list of reviews for a specific seller's products
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of product reviews associated with a specific seller's product catalog. This operation provides sellers with visibility into customer feedback across all their listed products, enabling them to monitor customer satisfaction, identify product issues, and respond to customer concerns.

The operation supports advanced filtering capabilities including rating ranges (1-5 stars), verified purchase status to show only reviews from confirmed buyers, review date ranges for temporal analysis, and product-specific filtering. Sellers can analyze review trends, identify top-rated and low-rated products, and track review sentiment over time.

Technical Implementation: Reviews are retrieved by joining the shopping_mall_reviews table with shopping_mall_sales to filter by seller ownership. The query filters reviews where the associated sale's seller_id matches the provided sellerId parameter. The implementation constructs the filter as: reviews.sale.seller_id = {sellerId}. Proper database indexing on shopping_mall_sales.shopping_mall_seller_id ensures efficient query performance.

Security considerations: This operation is restricted to authenticated seller accounts via the authorizationActor constraint. Sellers can only view reviews for their own products - the sellerId path parameter is validated against the authenticated seller's identity to prevent unauthorized access to other sellers' review data. The operation includes rate limiting to prevent abuse and implements pagination to handle large review datasets efficiently.

The response includes review summary information optimized for seller dashboards, containing review content, ratings, buyer information (anonymized as needed), product references, timestamps, and seller response status. This enables sellers to prioritize responding to reviews that haven't been addressed yet.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of review summary information for the seller's products matching the search criteria

current.description:
Current page number in the paginated result set.

This represents which page of results is currently being returned, using 1-based indexing where the first page is numbered 1. The value must be between 1 and the total number of pages (inclusive).

Clients use this value to understand their current position in the result set and to construct navigation to previous/next pages. When current equals 1, there are no previous pages. When current equals pages, there are no next pages.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records returned per page.

This defines the page size - how many individual records are included in each page of results. The actual number of records in the current page may be less than this limit on the final page of results.

This value controls the density of API responses and affects both performance and user experience. Common values range from 10 to 100 depending on the resource type and use case.

records.description:
Total number of records matching the query criteria.

This represents the complete count of records that match the current filter/search parameters, not just the records returned in the current page. This is the filtered subset of the database, not necessarily all records in the table.

Clients use this value to display total result counts to users and to calculate pagination controls. When combined with limit, it determines the total number of pages needed to display all matching results.

pages.description:
Total number of pages in the paginated result set.

This is calculated by dividing the total records by the limit (page size) and rounding up to the nearest integer (ceiling operation). For example, with 25 records and a limit of 10, pages would be 3 (pages 1 and 2 contain 10 records each, page 3 contains 5 records).

When there are no matching records, this value is 0. When there are records, this value is always at least 1. Clients use this to render pagination controls and to validate that requested page numbers are within valid bounds.

IPage.IPagination.description:
Pagination metadata providing information about the current page position and total result set size.

This structure is included in all paginated API responses to help clients navigate through large result sets. It contains four key metrics: the current page number, the page size limit, the total number of matching records, and the total number of pages available.

Clients use this metadata to implement pagination controls (previous/next buttons, page number selectors), display result counts to users, and validate navigation requests. The combination of these four values provides complete information needed to navigate any paginated result set.

access.description:
JWT access token for authenticated requests.

This token should be included in the Authorization header for subsequent
authenticated API requests as `Bearer {token}`.

refresh.description:
Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

This token can be used to request new access tokens when the current access
token expires, extending the user's session.

expired_at.description:
Access token expiration timestamp.

ISO 8601 date-time string indicating when the access token will expire and
can no longer be used for authentication.

refreshable_until.description:
Refresh token expiration timestamp.

ISO 8601 date-time string indicating the latest time until which the
refresh token can be used to obtain new access tokens.

IAuthorizationToken.description:
Authorization token response structure.

This interface defines the structure of the authorization token response
returned after successful user authentication. It contains both access and
refresh tokens along with their expiration information.

This token structure is automatically included in API schemas when the system
detects authorization actors in the requirements analysis phase. It provides
a standard format for JWT-based authentication across the generated backend
applications.

IPageIShoppingMallCategory.ISummary.description:
Paginated response wrapper for product category listings in the shopping mall marketplace.

This type encapsulates a single page of category results along with pagination metadata, enabling efficient retrieval and navigation of potentially large category hierarchies. Used as the response type for category search, filter, and browsing operations.

The pagination structure allows clients to retrieve category data in manageable chunks rather than loading entire category trees at once, improving performance and user experience. Clients can navigate through pages using the pagination metadata to request previous, next, first, or last pages.

Typically used in category list endpoints, hierarchical navigation operations, and administrative category management interfaces. The response combines the requested category data with navigation information needed to build pagination controls in user interfaces.

This wrapper type follows standard pagination patterns across the shopping mall API, providing consistent response structures for all paginated list operations. The pagination field contains standardized metadata while the data field holds the domain-specific category records.

pagination.description:
Pagination metadata for the product sale listing response.

Provides essential navigation information including current page number, records per page limit, total record count across all pages, and total number of pages available. Enables clients to build pagination controls and determine navigation possibilities.

Clients use this metadata to render page selectors, previous/next buttons, and page jump controls in product listing interfaces.

data.description:
Array of product sale summary records for the current page.

Contains the actual product listings matching the search and filter criteria, limited to the page size specified in the request. Each element provides essential product information including identifier, name, price, thumbnail image, seller reference, and category assignment.

The array length will be at most equal to the requested limit parameter, and may be smaller on the final page or when fewer products match the filter criteria.

IPageIShoppingMallSale.ISummary.description:
Paginated response wrapper for product sale listings in the shopping mall marketplace.

This type encapsulates a single page of product sale results along with comprehensive pagination metadata, enabling efficient retrieval and navigation through potentially large product catalogs. Serves as the standard response structure for product search, discovery, and inventory browsing operations.

Pagination prevents performance degradation and overwhelming data transfer by breaking large result sets into manageable pages. Buyers can browse products page-by-page, sellers can navigate their inventory in chunks, and admins can review marketplace listings systematically.

The response structure combines requested product data with navigation metadata needed to implement pagination controls in user interfaces. Clients can determine total result counts, current position within results, and availability of additional pages without making separate count queries.

Used extensively in product discovery endpoints including marketplace-wide searches, category-filtered browsing, seller-specific inventory views, and administrative product moderation interfaces. The pagination wrapper provides consistency across all product listing operations throughout the shopping mall API.

The standardized pagination structure enables client applications to implement reusable pagination components that work uniformly across different product listing contexts, improving development efficiency and user experience consistency.

pagination.description:
Pagination metadata for navigating through variant attribute result sets.

Provides information about the current page position, total pages available, total record count, and page size limits. Essential for implementing paginated navigation controls in variant attribute management interfaces.

data.description:
Array of variant attribute summary records for the current page.

Contains the actual variant attribute data matching the search criteria, with each element representing one variant dimension (such as Color, Size, or Material) configured for the product sale. Each attribute includes its available values that buyers can select.

IPageIShoppingMallSaleVariantAttribute.I.description:
Paginated response containing variant attribute summaries for a product sale listing.

This response wrapper combines pagination metadata with an array of variant attribute records from the shopping_mall_sale_variant_attributes table. Variant attributes define the configurable dimensions of a product (such as Color, Size, Material, Style) that buyers can select to customize their purchase.

Pagination is essential for products with complex variant configurations that may have multiple attributes (up to 3 per product). While individual products typically have 1-3 attributes, the pagination structure supports efficient data transfer and consistent API patterns across all listing operations.

Typical usage scenarios include:
- Product management interfaces where sellers configure variant options
- Buyer-facing product pages displaying available customization dimensions
- Variant configuration tools that allow filtering and searching attributes
- Administrative dashboards monitoring product variant structures

The paginated structure enables efficient handling of variant attribute queries with filtering, sorting, and search capabilities while maintaining reasonable response sizes and optimal client-side performance.

pagination.description:
Pagination metadata for navigating through variant value result sets.

Provides current page position, total available pages, total record count, and page size information. Critical for implementing pagination controls when managing variant values that may number in the dozens for attributes like Color or Size.

data.description:
Array of variant value summary records for the current page.

Contains the actual variant value options matching the search criteria. Each element represents one selectable option within a variant attribute (e.g., 'Red', 'Blue', 'Green' for a Color attribute, or 'S', 'M', 'L', 'XL' for a Size attribute). These values combine across attributes to generate the complete SKU matrix.

IPageIShoppingMallSaleVariantValue.ISumm.description:
Paginated response containing variant value summaries for a specific variant attribute within a product sale.

This response wrapper combines pagination metadata with an array of variant value records from the shopping_mall_sale_variant_values table. Variant values represent the individual selectable options within a variant attribute dimension - for example, specific colors (Red, Blue, Green) within a Color attribute, or sizes (S, M, L, XL) within a Size attribute.

Pagination is particularly important for variant values because a single attribute can contain up to 50 distinct values. Products with extensive option ranges (like detailed color palettes with 30+ shades, or comprehensive size charts with 20+ sizes) benefit from paginated loading to maintain responsive user interfaces and efficient data transfer.

Typical usage scenarios include:
- Seller variant configuration interfaces managing large value sets
- Product variant management tools with search and filtering for specific values
- SKU generation workflows that combine values across attributes
- Administrative monitoring of variant value completeness and organization
- Bulk value management operations with filtering and sorting

The paginated structure supports efficient handling of variant value queries with search, filtering by display order or creation date, and sorting capabilities. This ensures optimal performance even when managing products with complex variant configurations containing dozens of selectable options per attribute.

pagination.description:
Pagination metadata for the SKU variant result set.

Provides essential information about the current page position, total record count, and available pages for navigation. Enables clients to implement pagination controls and calculate total result set size without loading all records.

Includes current page number, records per page limit, total record count across all pages, and calculated total page count.

data.description:
Array of SKU variant summary records for the current page.

Contains the actual SKU variant data matching the search criteria and pagination parameters. Each element provides essential variant information including SKU code, pricing, variant attribute combination, and parent product reference.

The array length is controlled by the pagination limit parameter and may be smaller than the limit on the final page of results.

IPageIShoppingMallSaleSku.ISummary.description:
Paginated response container for product SKU variant search and listing operations.

This response structure wraps a collection of SKU variant summaries with pagination metadata, enabling efficient browsing of product variants across multiple pages. Essential for managing products with numerous variant combinations (e.g., products with multiple colors, sizes, and material options).

Used as the response type for SKU search and filtering operations where the total number of variants may exceed practical single-response limits. The pagination wrapper allows clients to retrieve results incrementally, improving performance and user experience when dealing with large variant catalogs.

The structure separates pagination control information from the actual data payload, following standard REST API pagination patterns. Clients use the pagination metadata to build navigation controls (previous/next page, page numbers, total count displays) while the data array contains the SKU summaries for the current page.

Typically returned by operations like PATCH /sales/{saleCode}/skus which retrieve filtered lists of product variants based on search criteria including variant attributes, price ranges, stock levels, and availability status.

pagination.description:
Pagination metadata for the product image result set.

Provides essential information about the current page position, total image count, and available pages for navigation. Enables clients to implement pagination controls and calculate total result set size for product image galleries.

Includes current page number, records per page limit, total image count across all pages, and calculated total page count.

data.description:
Array of product image summary records for the current page.

Contains the actual product image data matching the search and filter criteria. Each element provides essential image information including image URL, display order, primary flag, and upload timestamp.

The array length is controlled by the pagination limit parameter and may be smaller than the limit on the final page of results.

IPageIShoppingMallSaleImage.ISummary.description:
Paginated response container for product image search and gallery management operations.

This response structure wraps a collection of product image summaries with pagination metadata, enabling efficient browsing of product visual content across multiple pages. Essential for managing products with extensive image galleries where loading all images simultaneously would impact performance.

Used as the response type for product image listing and search operations where sellers or admins need to browse, organize, or moderate product visual assets. The pagination wrapper allows clients to retrieve images incrementally, which is particularly important for products with many high-resolution images.

The structure separates pagination control information from the actual image data payload, following standard REST API pagination patterns. Clients use the pagination metadata to build gallery navigation controls (previous/next page, thumbnail strips, image count displays) while the data array contains the image summaries for the current page.

Typically returned by operations like PATCH /sales/{saleCode}/images and PATCH /sales/{saleCode}/skus/{skuCode}/images which retrieve filtered lists of product images based on criteria including display order, primary image status, upload date ranges, and SKU variant associations. Supports efficient image gallery management in both seller dashboards and admin moderation interfaces.

pagination.description:
Pagination metadata providing navigation information for the question list.

Contains essential pagination details including current page number, page size limit, total record count, and total page count. This metadata enables clients to implement pagination controls, display page numbers, show total results, and navigate between pages of product questions.

Used by frontend components to render pagination UI elements such as page number buttons, next/previous controls, and result count displays. Essential for managing large question sets and providing smooth user experience when browsing product Q&A sections.

data.description:
Array of customer question summaries for the current page.

Contains lightweight question representations optimized for list display, including question content, buyer information, answer status, and submission timestamps. Each item provides enough information to render question cards in product Q&A sections without requiring additional API calls.

Typical page sizes range from 10 to 50 questions depending on UI design. For products with no questions, this array will be empty. The summary variant excludes full answer details to maintain performance; clients should fetch individual questions for complete answer threads.

IPageIShoppingMallSaleQuestion.ISummary.description:
Paginated collection of customer product questions with navigation metadata.

This response wrapper combines a list of question summaries with pagination information, enabling efficient browsing of customer inquiries about a product. Used when retrieving filtered and sorted question lists for product detail pages, seller dashboards, or customer service interfaces.

The pagination structure supports various UI patterns including traditional page-based navigation, infinite scroll implementations, and load-more buttons. Clients can use the pagination metadata to display page controls, show total question counts, and manage navigation state.

Typically returned from search and filter operations on product questions, this structure optimizes performance by limiting result set size while providing complete pagination context. Essential for products with extensive Q&A history where loading all questions at once would impact performance and user experience.

pagination.description:
Pagination metadata for navigating through historical snapshot timeline.

Provides essential navigation information including current page position, page size, total snapshot count, and total pages. Enables clients to implement timeline navigation controls, display snapshot counts, and manage historical data browsing for products with extensive change histories.

Particularly important for audit trail interfaces, dispute resolution tools, and compliance reporting where users need to navigate through potentially large sets of historical product states. Supports integration with date range filters and temporal queries for targeted snapshot analysis.

data.description:
Array of historical snapshot summaries showing product evolution over time.

Contains lightweight snapshot representations optimized for timeline displays, including snapshot timestamps, product status at capture time, and essential identification fields. Each summary provides enough context to render snapshot cards in history timelines without requiring full denormalized product data.

Typically ordered chronologically to visualize product changes over time. For newly created products with no modification history, this array will be empty. Summary variant excludes complete denormalized product details to maintain performance; clients should fetch individual snapshots for full historical state information needed in detailed audit views or dispute resolution scenarios.

IPageIShoppingMallSaleSnapshot.ISummary.description:
Paginated collection of historical product sale snapshots with timeline navigation metadata.

This response wrapper combines a chronologically ordered list of snapshot summaries with pagination information, enabling efficient browsing of product modification history. Used when retrieving audit trails for compliance monitoring, change tracking for dispute resolution, or historical analysis for seller performance evaluation.

The pagination structure supports various temporal navigation patterns including timeline scrubbing, date range filtering, and incremental history loading. Essential for products with extensive modification histories where loading complete snapshot data would impact system performance and response times.

Typically returned from snapshot search operations with date range filters and temporal sorting, this structure optimizes audit trail browsing while maintaining complete historical accuracy. Particularly valuable for administrative oversight, fraud investigation, and regulatory compliance scenarios requiring detailed product change tracking across the marketplace lifecycle.

pagination.description:
Pagination metadata for navigating through inventory transaction history.

Provides current page number, total records count, total pages, and page size limit. Essential for implementing pagination controls in inventory audit interfaces and transaction history views.

data.description:
Array of inventory transaction summary records for the current page.

Contains lightweight transaction data optimized for list displays and audit trail browsing. Each summary includes essential transaction details without full relationship data for improved performance.

IPageIShoppingMallInventoryTransaction.I.description:
Paginated collection of inventory transaction summary records.

Provides a performance-optimized view of inventory transaction history with pagination support for efficient browsing of large audit trails. Each page contains summary-level transaction data suitable for list displays, quick audits, and transaction history overviews.

The ISummary variant is used to minimize payload size when displaying transaction lists, including only essential fields like transaction type, quantity change, and timestamps without loading complete relationship data for SKUs, orders, and sellers.

This structure supports efficient navigation through potentially large transaction histories spanning multiple SKUs, sellers, and time periods. The pagination metadata enables implementation of page controls, infinite scrolling, and batch processing of transaction records.

Typically used in inventory audit dashboards, transaction history lists, reconciliation interfaces, and reporting tools where users need to browse and filter large volumes of inventory movements without requiring complete transaction details upfront.

pagination.description:
Pagination metadata for navigating through complete inventory transaction records.

Provides current page number, total records count, total pages, and page size limit. Essential for implementing pagination controls in detailed inventory analysis and comprehensive audit reporting.

data.description:
Array of complete inventory transaction records for the current page.

Contains full transaction data including relationships to SKUs, orders, and sellers. Each record provides comprehensive audit trail information for detailed analysis and investigation.

IPageIShoppingMallInventoryTransaction.description:
Paginated collection of complete inventory transaction records with full relationship data.

Provides comprehensive inventory transaction history with pagination support for detailed analysis, audit investigations, and in-depth reconciliation. Each page contains complete transaction records including all relationships to product SKUs, orders, and sellers, along with full transaction metadata.

The full entity variant is used when detailed transaction analysis is required, such as investigating specific inventory discrepancies, performing comprehensive audits, generating detailed reports, or analyzing transaction patterns with complete context about related entities.

Each transaction record includes the complete before-and-after inventory quantities, quantity change deltas, transaction types (addition, reduction, sale, cancellation, return, adjustment, reconciliation), optional reason explanations, and immutable timestamps. Relationships to product SKU variants, triggering orders (when applicable), and seller accounts (for manual adjustments) provide complete audit trail context.

This structure supports detailed inventory movement investigations, financial audits, seller analytics, and system reconciliation processes. The pagination enables efficient handling of large transaction datasets while providing access to complete information needed for thorough analysis and reporting.

Typically used in detailed inventory audit interfaces, discrepancy investigation tools, comprehensive reporting systems, and reconciliation workflows where complete transaction context including all relationships is essential for accurate analysis.

pagination.description:
Pagination metadata for the inventory reservation result set.

Provides essential pagination information including current page number, page size limit, total record count, and total pages. This metadata enables clients to implement pagination controls and navigate through large sets of inventory reservation records efficiently.

data.description:
Array of inventory reservation records matching the search criteria.

Contains the actual reservation data for the current page, with each element representing a temporary inventory hold during the checkout process. The array size is constrained by the pagination limit parameter and may be empty if no reservations match the specified filters.

IPageIShoppingMallInventoryReservation.description:
Paginated response wrapper for inventory reservation records.

This response type encapsulates a page of inventory reservation results along with pagination metadata. It follows the standard pagination pattern used throughout the API, providing both the data payload and the information needed to navigate through multiple pages of results.

Inventory reservations represent temporary holds on product SKU inventory created during the buyer checkout process. These reservations prevent overselling by allocating specific quantities to buyers who are completing their purchases. The reservation system is critical for maintaining accurate inventory availability and ensuring a smooth checkout experience.

The pagination structure contains two primary components: the `pagination` metadata object providing navigation information (current page, total records, total pages, page size), and the `data` array containing the actual inventory reservation records for the current page. This separation enables efficient data transfer while maintaining complete pagination state.

This paginated response is returned by inventory reservation search operations used by sellers to monitor reservations for their products and administrators to oversee platform-wide reservation activity. The underlying data comes from the shopping_mall_inventory_reservations table in the Prisma schema, which tracks all temporary inventory allocations.

Typical use cases include monitoring active reservations to understand current inventory commitment levels, identifying expired or stuck reservations that may need cleanup, analyzing checkout funnel metrics through reservation completion rates, and troubleshooting inventory availability issues by examining reservation patterns.

pagination.description:
Pagination metadata for the shopping cart item result set.

Provides essential pagination information including current page number, page size limit, total record count, and total pages. This metadata enables buyers to navigate through their cart contents efficiently, especially important for buyers with large carts containing many items.

data.description:
Array of shopping cart item summaries matching the search and filter criteria.

Contains lightweight cart item representations for the current page, with each element including essential product information, quantity, and pricing. The array size is constrained by the pagination limit parameter and may be empty if no items match the specified filters or if the cart is empty.

IPageIShoppingMallCartItem.ISummary.description:
Paginated response wrapper for shopping cart item summaries.

This response type encapsulates a page of shopping cart item results along with pagination metadata. It follows the standard pagination pattern used throughout the API, providing both the data payload and the navigation information needed to browse through multiple pages of cart contents.

Shopping cart items represent products that authenticated buyers have added to their carts with the intent to purchase. Each cart item links a specific product SKU variant to a buyer along with the desired quantity. The cart persists across sessions, allowing buyers to accumulate items over time before proceeding to checkout.

The pagination structure contains two primary components: the `pagination` metadata object providing navigation information (current page, total items in cart, total pages, items per page), and the `data` array containing lightweight summary representations of cart items for the current page. This separation enables efficient cart display while maintaining complete pagination state for large carts.

This paginated response is returned by cart search and retrieval operations, enabling buyers to view, filter, and manage their shopping cart contents. The underlying data comes from the shopping_mall_cart_items table in the Prisma schema. The summary format includes essential cart item information without excessive detail, optimized for cart list displays.

Typical use cases include displaying the buyer's current cart contents with product details and pricing, filtering cart items by category or price range to help buyers organize large carts, sorting items by various criteria such as date added or price, and implementing search functionality to help buyers quickly find specific items within their cart.

pagination.description: Page information.

data.description: List of records.

IPageIShoppingMallWishlistItem.ISummary.description:
Paginated response wrapper for wishlist item search results.

This paginated collection contains wishlist items that authenticated buyers have saved for future purchase consideration. The response structure includes both the wishlist item data array and pagination metadata for navigating through the buyer's complete wishlist when it contains more items than the requested page size.

The pagination field provides essential navigation information including the current page number, items per page limit, total record count across all pages, and total page count. This metadata enables frontend applications to render pagination controls, display result counts, and calculate result ranges.

The data array contains IShoppingMallWishlistItem.ISummary objects optimized for list display, showing essential product details, pricing information, availability status, and when items were added to the wishlist. Each summary includes embedded product SKU and sale information through nested references, providing sufficient context for buyers to evaluate their saved items without additional API calls.

This response type is used by the wishlist search operation to return filtered and sorted wishlist results based on buyer-specified criteria such as product name, category, price range, or date added. The paginated structure ensures performant responses even for buyers with extensive wishlists approaching the 200-item maximum limit.

pagination.description: Page information.

data.description: List of records.

IPageIShoppingMallBuyerAddress.description:
Paginated response wrapper for buyer delivery address search results.

This paginated collection contains delivery addresses from the authenticated buyer's address book. The response structure includes both the complete address data array and pagination metadata for navigating through the buyer's saved addresses when filtering or browsing their address book.

The pagination field provides navigation information including current page number, items per page limit, total address count, and total page count. Since buyers can maintain up to 10 delivery addresses and most have fewer addresses, pagination is less critical than for product catalogs, but the structure supports scalability and consistent API patterns.

The data array contains complete IShoppingMallBuyerAddress objects with full postal address information, recipient contact details, custom labels, delivery preferences, and address metadata. Each address record includes all fields necessary for order checkout, shipping label generation, and address book management without requiring additional API requests.

This response type is used by the address search operation to return filtered and sorted address results based on buyer-specified criteria such as address type (residential/commercial), address label, default status, or text search across address fields. The paginated structure maintains consistency with other search operations across the platform while accommodating the typically smaller result sets of address book queries.

Address data returned in this structure is used during checkout for delivery address selection, in buyer account management interfaces for maintaining the address book, and for identifying the default shipping address for streamlined purchasing workflows.

pagination.description:
Pagination metadata for the order list.

Provides information about the current page position, total records, and navigation details for browsing through the complete order dataset.

data.description:
Array of order summary records for the current page.

Contains the order records matching the search criteria and filters, limited to the current page size. Each item provides essential order information optimized for list displays.

IPageIShoppingMallOrder.ISummary.description:
Paginated response containing a list of order summaries.

This wrapper type encapsulates both the order data and pagination metadata for list retrieval operations. It enables efficient navigation through large order datasets by dividing results into manageable pages.

Used as the response type for order search and list operations across buyer, seller, and admin contexts. The pagination information allows clients to implement paging controls and display total record counts.

The structure follows the standard IPage pattern used throughout the API for consistent pagination behavior across all list endpoints.

pagination.description:
Pagination metadata for the seller segment list.

Provides information about the current page position, total seller segments, and navigation details for browsing through all seller portions of an order.

data.description:
Array of seller segment summary records for the current page.

Contains the seller sub-order records matching the search criteria, limited to the current page size. Each item provides essential seller portion information including fulfillment status and financial breakdowns.

IPageIShoppingMallOrderSeller.ISummary.description:
Paginated response containing a list of order seller segment summaries.

This wrapper type encapsulates both the seller segment data and pagination metadata for retrieving seller portions within a multi-seller order. It enables efficient navigation when an order contains items from many different sellers.

Used as the response type for seller segment search operations within a specific parent order. The pagination information allows clients to implement paging controls when displaying how an order is distributed across multiple sellers.

The structure follows the standard IPage pattern used throughout the API for consistent pagination behavior across all list endpoints.

pagination.description:
Pagination metadata for the order items result set.

Provides essential information about the current page position, total records, and navigation capabilities.
Includes current page number, page size limit, total record count, and total page count for implementing pagination controls in order detail interfaces.

data.description:
Array of order item summary records matching the search criteria.

Contains the actual order item data for the current page, with each element representing one line item from the order.
Includes essential product information, pricing, quantity, and fulfillment status for display in order detail views and seller dashboards.

IPageIShoppingMallOrderItem.ISummary.description:
Paginated response containing order item summary records for a specific order.

This wrapper type encapsulates search results for order items within an order, providing both the data records and pagination metadata needed for list displays and navigation.
Used as the response type for order item search operations where buyers, sellers, or administrators need to view and filter items within a specific order.

The pagination structure enables efficient handling of orders containing many items by breaking results into manageable pages.
This is particularly important for bulk orders or marketplace orders with items from multiple sellers where the item count can be substantial.

Typical use cases include order detail pages showing all purchased items, seller dashboards displaying items they need to fulfill, and admin interfaces for order management and dispute resolution.
The search capabilities integrated with this paginated response allow filtering by product name, SKU, price ranges, and seller to quickly locate specific items within large orders.

pagination.description:
Pagination metadata for the status history result set.

Provides essential information about the current page position within the complete audit trail, total status change records, and navigation capabilities.
Includes current page number, page size limit, total record count, and total page count for implementing timeline navigation controls.

data.description:
Array of status history records representing order state transitions.

Contains chronologically ordered status change events for the current page, with each element capturing one transition in the order lifecycle.
Includes status type, transition timestamp, and optional notes for displaying complete audit trails in timeline interfaces and compliance reports.

IPageIShoppingMallOrderStatusHistory.ISu.description:
Paginated response containing order status history records for audit trail and tracking purposes.

This wrapper type encapsulates the complete status transition history for a specific order, providing both the chronological event records and pagination metadata needed for timeline displays and compliance reporting.
Used as the response type for status history queries where buyers track order progress, sellers monitor fulfillment workflows, and administrators investigate order issues or disputes.

The pagination structure enables efficient navigation through potentially long order histories, especially for orders with complex fulfillment paths involving multiple status changes, cancellations, or refund processes.
This is critical for compliance requirements where complete audit trails must be maintained and accessible without performance degradation.

Typical use cases include order tracking pages showing delivery progress, customer service interfaces investigating order issues, dispute resolution systems analyzing order timelines, and compliance reporting extracting status change patterns.
The filtering capabilities integrated with this paginated response allow searching by specific status types, date ranges, and actors to analyze particular aspects of the order lifecycle for operational analytics and regulatory compliance.

pagination.description:
Pagination metadata providing information about the current page position, total records, and navigation context.

Includes the current page number, page size limit, total record count across all pages, and calculated total page count. This metadata enables clients to implement pagination controls, display page position indicators, and calculate whether previous/next page navigation is available.

Essential for building user-friendly list interfaces that handle large datasets efficiently.

data.description:
Array of order cancellation request summary records matching the search and filter criteria.

Each element provides essential cancellation information including the cancellation ID, reason code, approval status, refund amount, request timestamp, and summary references to the associated order and requesting actor (buyer or seller).

The array length is controlled by the pagination limit parameter and may be empty if no cancellations match the specified criteria. Array ordering is determined by the sort_by and order parameters from the request.

IPageIShoppingMallOrderCancellation.ISum.description:
Paginated response wrapper containing a list of order cancellation request summaries with pagination metadata.

This type represents the standard paginated response format for order cancellation list operations. It combines an array of cancellation summary records with comprehensive pagination information, enabling efficient navigation through potentially large result sets from the shopping_mall_order_cancellations table.

Used as the response type for administrative cancellation search and retrieval operations, particularly the PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/cancellations endpoint. The pagination structure supports configurable page sizes, multi-field sorting, and complex filtering criteria including cancellation status, order identifiers, buyer information, and date ranges.

The data array contains lightweight summary representations optimized for list displays, providing essential cancellation details without the complete approval workflow history or detailed admin notes. Clients can use the pagination metadata to implement page navigation controls and display result position information to users.

pagination.description:
Pagination metadata providing information about the current page position, total records, and navigation context.

Includes the current page number, page size limit, total record count across all pages, and calculated total page count. This metadata enables clients to implement pagination controls, display page position indicators, and calculate whether previous/next page navigation is available.

Essential for building user-friendly list interfaces that handle large datasets efficiently.

data.description:
Array of refund request summary records matching the search and filter criteria.

Each element provides essential refund request information including the request ID, tracking number, refund reason category, requested amount, approval status, and submission timestamp.

The array length is controlled by the pagination limit parameter and may be empty if no refund requests match the specified criteria. Array ordering is determined by the sort_by and sort_order parameters from the request.

IPageIShoppingMallRefundRequest.ISummary.description:
Paginated response wrapper containing a list of refund request summaries with pagination metadata.

This type represents the standard paginated response format for refund request list operations. It combines an array of refund request summary records with comprehensive pagination information, enabling efficient navigation through potentially large result sets from the shopping_mall_refund_requests table.

Used as the response type for administrative refund request search and management operations, particularly the PATCH /shoppingMall/admin/refundRequests endpoint. The pagination structure supports configurable page sizes, multi-field sorting, and complex filtering criteria including buyer, order, approval status, amount ranges, date ranges, and full-text search on refund reasons and notes.

The data array contains lightweight summary representations optimized for administrative dashboards and queue management interfaces, providing essential refund request details without the complete approval workflow history or detailed admin decision notes. Clients can use the pagination metadata to implement page navigation controls and display result position information to administrators reviewing refund requests.

pagination.description:
Pagination metadata for the payment method query results.

Provides essential information for navigating through the complete set of payment methods including current page number, total pages, records per page, and total record count. This metadata enables clients to implement pagination controls such as page number selectors, next/previous buttons, and result count displays.

The pagination object works in conjunction with the data array to provide a complete view of where the current result set fits within the overall query results.

data.description:
Array of payment method summary records matching the search criteria.

Contains the actual payment method data for the current page, with each element representing a saved payment method belonging to the authenticated buyer. The array length is determined by the pagination limit parameter and may be smaller than the limit on the final page of results.

Each payment method summary includes essential identification information such as payment type, masked card details, and verification status, providing sufficient information for buyers to recognize and select payment methods during checkout or account management workflows.

IPageIShoppingMallPaymentMethod.ISummary.description:
Paginated response wrapper for buyer payment method queries.

This schema represents the complete response structure for payment method search operations, combining pagination metadata with an array of payment method summaries. It enables efficient retrieval and display of potentially large sets of saved payment methods while maintaining reasonable response sizes and optimal performance.

Used as the response type for buyer payment method search endpoints, this wrapper supports various use cases including checkout payment method selection, account settings management, and payment method maintenance workflows. The pagination structure allows buyers with many saved payment methods to navigate through their complete payment method list efficiently.

The schema follows the standard pagination pattern used throughout the shopping mall platform, ensuring consistent client-side pagination implementation across different resource types.

pagination.description:
Pagination metadata for the payment transaction query results.

Provides essential navigation information including current page number, total pages available, records per page limit, and total transaction count matching the search criteria. This metadata enables clients to implement comprehensive pagination controls for navigating through potentially large transaction datasets spanning multiple pages.

Critical for financial reporting and audit trail interfaces where users need to navigate through extensive transaction histories while maintaining performance and usability. The pagination metadata works in conjunction with the transaction data array to provide complete context about result set positioning.

data.description:
Array of payment transaction summary records for the current page.

Contains the actual transaction data matching the search filters, with each element representing a payment transaction record from the shopping_mall_payment_transactions table. The array length is determined by the pagination limit and may be smaller than the limit on the final page.

Each transaction summary includes key transaction details such as transaction type (authorization, capture, void, refund), payment amount, currency, processing status, payment provider, and transaction timestamp. This provides sufficient information for displaying transaction history, financial reporting, dispute resolution, and audit trail reviews without exposing sensitive payment card details in compliance with PCI standards.

IPageIShoppingMallPaymentTransaction.ISu.description:
Paginated response wrapper for payment transaction search queries.

This schema represents the complete response structure for payment transaction retrieval operations, combining pagination metadata with an array of transaction summaries. It supports efficient querying and display of potentially extensive transaction histories while maintaining optimal response sizes and system performance.

Used across multiple actor contexts including buyer payment history views, seller revenue tracking dashboards, and administrator financial audit interfaces. The pagination wrapper enables different user types to navigate through their relevant transaction subsets based on their authorization scope and search filters.

Each actor sees filtered transaction data appropriate to their role: buyers view their own order payments, sellers see transactions for their products, and administrators access platform-wide transaction records for financial oversight and dispute resolution. The consistent pagination structure ensures uniform client-side implementation regardless of actor type or search complexity.

pagination.description:
Page information.

Contains current page number, page size limit, total record count, and total page count for navigating through the complete refund transaction dataset.

data.description:
List of refund transaction summary records.

Array of refund transaction summaries matching the search criteria, containing essential information about refund payment processing including transaction IDs, amounts, status, and timestamps.

IPageIShoppingMallRefundTransaction.ISum.description:
Paginated response wrapper for refund transaction search results.

This response structure wraps filtered refund transaction summaries with pagination metadata, enabling efficient navigation through large datasets of refund payment processing records. Used by administrative dashboards and financial reporting interfaces to display refund transaction lists with proper pagination controls.

The pagination object provides navigation information including current page position, page size configuration, total record count across all pages, and calculated total page count. The data array contains the actual refund transaction summaries for the current page, each providing essential refund details without full audit information.

This structure supports the refund transaction search operations on the shopping_mall_refund_transactions table, allowing administrators and authorized users to browse through refund processing history with filtering by status, amount ranges, payment providers, and temporal criteria. The pagination enables handling of large refund transaction datasets spanning multiple orders, buyers, and settlement periods.

Typical usage includes admin financial reconciliation dashboards, refund status monitoring interfaces, payment provider reconciliation reports, and customer support tools for tracking refund processing. The paginated structure ensures responsive performance even with extensive refund transaction histories.

pagination.description:
Page information.

Contains current page number, page size limit, total record count, and total page count for navigating through the complete seller payout dataset.

data.description:
List of seller payout summary records.

Array of seller payout summaries matching the search criteria, containing essential information about earnings settlements including payout IDs, settlement periods, net amounts, status, and processing timestamps.

IPageIShoppingMallSellerPayout.ISummary.description:
Paginated response wrapper for seller payout search results.
