Total inventory quantity including both available and reserved units.

Represents the complete stock level for this SKU variant before accounting for reservations. This is the absolute inventory count that the seller has physically available, updated through inventory transactions including restocks, manual adjustments, and inventory corrections.

Must be a non-negative integer. This value serves as the foundation for calculating available_quantity (total_quantity minus reserved_quantity).

reserved_quantity.description:
Quantity currently reserved during checkout processes.

Represents inventory that has been temporarily allocated to pending orders but not yet confirmed as sold. These are units held during the checkout process to prevent overselling while buyers complete their purchase.

This value increases when orders are placed and decreases when orders are fulfilled, cancelled, or reservations expire. Must be non-negative and cannot exceed total_quantity.

available_quantity.description:
Calculated available quantity for immediate purchase.

Derived value computed as (total_quantity minus reserved_quantity), representing the actual inventory available for new customer purchases. This is the quantity displayed to buyers in product listings and used in availability checks during checkout.

When this value reaches zero, the SKU becomes unavailable for purchase until restocked. This field is automatically recalculated whenever total_quantity or reserved_quantity changes.

low_stock_threshold.description:
Seller-configured threshold triggering low stock alerts.

When available_quantity falls below or equals this value, the system notifies sellers to restock. This threshold helps sellers maintain adequate inventory levels and avoid stockouts.

Default value is 10 units if not configured by the seller. Sellers can customize this threshold based on their restocking lead times and sales velocity.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this inventory stock record was first created.

Records when inventory tracking was initially established for this SKU variant, typically when the seller first listed the product variant or added inventory for a newly created SKU.

This timestamp is immutable and provides the baseline for tracking the inventory record's age and history.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this inventory stock record was last modified.

Updated whenever quantity changes occur through restocking, sales, reservations, manual adjustments, or threshold modifications. Used for tracking inventory change frequency, cache invalidation, and audit purposes.

This field helps identify stale inventory data and supports real-time inventory synchronization across the platform.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for archived inventory records.

When set, indicates the inventory record has been archived but preserved for historical data integrity and audit trails. Soft-deleted records are excluded from active inventory queries but remain accessible for reporting and historical analysis.

Typically set when a SKU variant is discontinued or removed from the catalog, allowing the platform to maintain complete transaction history while hiding the SKU from active inventory management.

IShoppingMallInventoryStock.description:
Current inventory stock levels for each product SKU variant.

Tracks the real-time available quantity for each SKU across the platform. This entity maintains the single source of truth for how many units of each product variant are currently in stock and available for purchase.

Every SKU must have a corresponding inventory stock record to support purchase operations. When buyers add items to cart or place orders, the system validates against these stock levels to prevent overselling. Stock quantities are updated through inventory transactions (additions, sales, returns, adjustments).

The available quantity is calculated as total quantity minus reserved quantity. Reserved quantities represent units in pending checkouts that are temporarily held but not yet sold. Low stock thresholds trigger seller alerts when inventory falls below configured levels.

This table integrates with the order management system for inventory deduction on sales and restoration on cancellations. It provides real-time availability data to the product catalog for displaying stock status to buyers.

IShoppingMallSaleImage.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering criteria for retrieving paginated lists of product images associated with sale listings.

This schema defines the query parameters for advanced product image searches. It supports filtering by display order, image status, creation date ranges, and various metadata attributes. The schema enables sellers to efficiently manage large product image galleries and admins to moderate visual content across the platform.

Pagination and sorting capabilities ensure optimal performance when handling sales with extensive image collections. The search functionality is essential for organizing product presentations, reordering image galleries, and maintaining visual consistency across product listings.

page.description:
Page number for pagination, starting from 1.

Specifies which page of results to retrieve in the paginated response. Combined with limit to implement efficient data pagination for large image collections.

limit.description:
Maximum number of image records to return per page.

Controls the page size for pagination. Platform enforces a maximum limit to prevent performance issues. Typical values range from 10-50 for seller dashboards and 20-100 for admin panels.

sort.description:
Array of sort criteria in format 'field:direction' (e.g., ['display_order:asc', 'created_at:desc']).

Specifies sorting rules for the result set. Multiple sort fields are applied in array order. Direction can be 'asc' (ascending) or 'desc' (descending). Common sort fields include display_order, created_at, file_size.

search.description:
General search term for full-text search across image metadata fields.

Searches across alt_text, description, and other textual image metadata. Useful for finding images by descriptive content or keywords.

shopping_mall_sale_sku_id.description:
Filter for images by their SKU variant association status.

When set to a specific UUID value, returns only images that are associated with that particular SKU variant (variant-specific images). This is useful for viewing images that appear only when buyers select a specific product configuration.

When explicitly set to null, returns only product-level images that are not associated with any specific SKU variant (images shared across all variants). These are typically the main product photos shown before variant selection.

When this parameter is omitted entirely from the request, the filter is not applied and all images are returned regardless of their SKU association status. This is the default behavior for general image gallery management.

display_order_min.description:
Minimum display order value for filtering images.

Filters images with display_order greater than or equal to this value. Useful for retrieving images positioned later in the gallery sequence.

display_order_max.description:
Maximum display order value for filtering images.

Filters images with display_order less than or equal to this value. Combined with display_order_min to retrieve specific ranges within the image gallery.

is_primary.description:
Filter for primary/main product image status.

When true, returns only the primary product image (typically the first image shown). When false, returns non-primary images. When omitted, returns all images regardless of primary status.

created_at_min.description:
Minimum creation timestamp for filtering images (ISO 8601 format).

Filters images created on or after this timestamp. Useful for finding recently uploaded images or images added within specific time periods.

created_at_max.description:
Maximum creation timestamp for filtering images (ISO 8601 format).

Filters images created on or before this timestamp. Combined with created_at_min to retrieve images uploaded within specific date ranges.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the sale image record.

This is the primary key auto-generated by the system when the image record is created in the shopping_mall_sale_images table. Follows UUID v4 format for globally unique identification.

Used to reference specific product images in API operations, relationships, and when performing image management actions like updates or deletions.

shopping_mall_sale_id.description:
Foreign key reference to the parent sale listing to which this image belongs.

This field establishes the relationship between the image and its parent product sale in the shopping_mall_sales table. Every product image must be associated with exactly one sale listing, making this a required non-nullable field.

Used in database queries to retrieve all images for a specific product, enforce referential integrity, and maintain the image-to-product relationship. When the parent sale is deleted, cascade rules determine whether associated images are also removed.

shopping_mall_sale_sku_id.description:
Optional foreign key reference to a specific SKU variant within the sale.

When this field is null, the image is a product-level image that applies to all SKU variants of the sale. These are typically the main product photos shown before a buyer selects specific variant options.

When this field contains a UUID value, the image is SKU-specific and should be displayed only when that particular variant is selected. For example, a clothing product might have different images for each color variant, where each color SKU has its own set of variant-specific photos.

This field enables the system to provide accurate visual representation based on the buyer's selected product configuration, improving the shopping experience by showing exactly what the chosen variant looks like.

url_original.description:
URL to original uploaded image without compression or resizing.

This is the highest quality version stored exactly as uploaded by the seller. Serves as the source for generating all size variants during image processing.

Typically used for high-resolution displays, print materials, or when maximum image quality is required. File size is largest among all variants.

url_large.description:
URL to large image variant optimized at 1600x1600 pixels.

Used for product page main display and zoom functionality. Provides high-quality visualization while maintaining reasonable file size for web delivery.

Generated automatically during image upload processing. Maintains aspect ratio with maximum dimension of 1600 pixels.

url_medium.description:
URL to medium image variant optimized at 800x800 pixels.

Used for product page gallery thumbnails and medium-sized displays. Balances quality and performance for typical product browsing scenarios.

Generated automatically during image upload processing. Maintains aspect ratio with maximum dimension of 800 pixels.

url_small.description:
URL to small image variant optimized at 400x400 pixels.

Used for product listings, search results, and category browsing where many products are displayed simultaneously. Optimized for fast loading and reduced bandwidth consumption.

Generated automatically during image upload processing. Maintains aspect ratio with maximum dimension of 400 pixels.

url_thumbnail.description:
URL to thumbnail image variant optimized at 150x150 pixels.

Used for shopping cart displays, order history, and compact UI components where space is limited. Smallest file size for maximum performance.

Generated automatically during image upload processing. Maintains aspect ratio with maximum dimension of 150 pixels.

is_primary.description:
Flag indicating whether this is the primary product image.

The primary image is the main representative image shown in product listings, search results, and as the default image in product galleries. Only one image per product should have this flag set to true.

When buyers first view a product, the primary image is displayed. Sellers should designate their best product photo as primary.

display_order.description:
Display sequence order for image gallery presentation.

Controls the position of this image within the product's image gallery. Lower numbers appear first, with 0 typically being the primary image position.

Sellers can reorder images by updating this value. Frontend displays images sorted by display_order ascending.

alt_text.description:
Alternative text for accessibility compliance and SEO optimization.

Describes the image content for screen readers (accessibility) and search engine indexing. Should be descriptive and meaningful, explaining what the image shows.

Optional but strongly recommended for accessibility standards and improved search visibility. When null, frontend may generate alt text from product name.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the image was uploaded to the system.

Recorded in ISO 8601 format with timezone information. Automatically set by the system during image creation.

Used for audit trails, tracking when images were added to products, and sorting images by upload date.

IShoppingMallSaleImage.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary representation of product sale images for list views and embeddings.

This summary DTO provides comprehensive image information including all size variants needed for responsive display across different contexts. Contains URLs for original and all processed image sizes (large, medium, small, thumbnail) to support optimal image delivery based on display requirements.

Used in product listing pages, search results, and anywhere product images need to be shown. The multiple URL variants enable frontend applications to select appropriate image sizes for different screen resolutions and use cases, optimizing both visual quality and performance.

Contains display order and primary flag for proper gallery sequencing and featured image identification. Includes optional alt text for accessibility compliance and SEO benefits.

Excludes relations to parent sale entity to prevent circular references and maintain lightweight payload size. Typically embedded in product sale DTOs as an array to show the complete image gallery.

Ideal for scenarios where multiple products with their images are displayed simultaneously, such as category browsing or search results, allowing efficient image loading with appropriate size selection.

shopping_mall_sale_sku_id.description:
Specific SKU variant to which this image applies.

When provided, associates this image with a specific product variant (color, size, etc.). Null for product-level images shared across all variants. This allows different SKU variants to have their own dedicated imagery, helping buyers visualize the exact variant they're considering.

When a SKU has specific images, those display when buyers select that variant. When a SKU has no specific images, the system falls back to product-level images.

url_original.description:
URL to original uploaded image.

Highest quality version stored without compression. This is the source image from which all other size variants are generated during image processing. Should point to the pre-uploaded file in the storage system (S3, CDN, etc.).

url_large.description:
URL to large image variant (1600x1600 pixels).

Used for product page main display and zoom functionality. This size provides high-quality detail when buyers want to examine product features closely. Generated automatically during image processing from the original upload.

url_medium.description:
URL to medium image variant (800x800 pixels).

Used for product page gallery thumbnails and general product displays. This size balances quality and performance for typical product browsing scenarios. Generated automatically during image processing.

url_small.description:
URL to small image variant (400x400 pixels).

Used for product listings and search results where space is limited. This size ensures fast loading while maintaining acceptable visual quality for browsing. Generated automatically during image processing.

url_thumbnail.description:
URL to thumbnail image variant (150x150 pixels).

Used for cart and order history displays where compact representation is needed. This smallest variant ensures minimal bandwidth usage in list contexts. Generated automatically during image processing.

is_primary.description:
Whether this is the primary image displayed first in galleries and listings.

Only one image per product or SKU should be marked as primary. The primary image serves as the main product thumbnail in search results, category listings, and appears first in product galleries. Critical for first-impression product presentation.

display_order.description:
Display sequence order for image gallery presentation.

Lower numbers appear first. Controls the sequence of images in product galleries beyond the primary image. Typically sequential starting from 0 (primary) to organize the visual story of the product effectively.

alt_text.description:
Alternative text for accessibility compliance and SEO.

Describes image content for screen readers and search engines. Should be concise but descriptive (e.g., 'Red leather handbag front view'). Following WCAG accessibility guidelines, meaningful alt text helps visually impaired users understand product imagery and improves SEO discoverability.

IShoppingMallSaleImage.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating new product sale images with multi-resolution URL variants.

This schema defines the data required to add a new image to a product sale listing. It follows the platform's image processing pipeline where uploaded images are processed into multiple size variants optimized for different display contexts (zoom, gallery, listings, thumbnails).

The parent sale context (shopping_mall_sale_id) is automatically determined from the path parameter (saleCode), so it's not included in the request body. When the authenticated seller creates the image, their seller ID is extracted from the JWT token and validated against the sale's ownership.

Required fields include all five URL variants (original, large, medium, small, thumbnail) generated during image processing, the is_primary flag to designate the main product image, and display_order for gallery sequencing. The system generates size variants automatically during upload, so all URL fields must be provided with references to the processed images.

Business rules enforced during creation include maximum image count limits per sale (typically 10-20 images), acceptable image formats (JPEG, PNG, WebP), minimum resolution requirements for the original image, and ensuring only one primary image exists per product or SKU. The operation validates that the referenced sale exists and is in a state that allows image uploads.

url_original.description:
URL to original uploaded image.

Highest quality version stored without compression. Update this when replacing the source image. Updating the original may trigger regeneration of all size variants to maintain consistency across the multi-resolution image set.

url_large.description:
URL to large image variant (1600x1600 pixels).

Used for product page main display and zoom. Update this when the large size variant changes, typically after reprocessing the original image with different quality settings or dimensions.

url_medium.description:
URL to medium image variant (800x800 pixels).

Used for product page gallery thumbnails. Update this when the medium size variant changes during image reprocessing or quality optimization.

url_small.description:
URL to small image variant (400x400 pixels).

Used for product listings and search results. Update this when the small size variant changes during image processing or CDN migration.

url_thumbnail.description:
URL to thumbnail image variant (150x150 pixels).

Used for cart and order history displays. Update this when the thumbnail variant changes during image processing or storage optimization.

is_primary.description:
Whether this is the primary image displayed first in galleries and listings.

Update this to change which image serves as the main product thumbnail. Only one image per product or SKU should be primary, so setting this to true should unset is_primary on other images in the same context.

display_order.description:
Display sequence order for image gallery presentation.

Update this to reorganize the product image gallery. Lower numbers appear first. Changing display order affects how buyers perceive the product's visual narrative and feature presentation.

alt_text.description:
Alternative text for accessibility compliance and SEO.

Update this to improve accessibility or SEO. Describes image content for screen readers and search engines. Should be concise but descriptive to help visually impaired users and improve search discoverability.

IShoppingMallSaleImage.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating product sale image metadata and properties with multi-resolution support.

This schema defines the modifiable properties of a product image, including all five URL variants (original, large, medium, small, thumbnail), the primary image designation, display order position, and alternative text for accessibility. All fields are optional to support partial updates, allowing sellers to modify only specific image attributes without affecting others.

The multi-resolution URL structure supports the platform's responsive image delivery system. When updating URL fields, ensure all variants remain consistent and point to the same logical image at different resolutions. Updating the original URL may require regenerating all size variants to maintain visual consistency.

The is_primary flag controls which image appears as the main product thumbnail in listings and galleries. The display_order field organizes the image sequence for product storytelling. Alternative text enhances accessibility and SEO by providing textual descriptions.

This update schema integrates with the shopping_mall_sale_images table structure, enabling sellers to maintain and optimize their product visual presentations while ensuring proper responsive image delivery and metadata for search engines and assistive technologies.

limit.description:
Maximum number of question records to return per page.

Controls the page size for paginated question list results. Accepts values between 1 and 100 questions per page.

Lower values improve response time and initial rendering performance. Higher values reduce the number of requests needed to browse all questions. Typical values range from 10-50 for optimal user experience.

page.description:
Page number for pagination, starting from 1.

Specifies which page of question results to retrieve when the total result set exceeds the limit. Page numbering is 1-indexed, meaning the first page is page 1, not page 0.

Combined with limit to calculate the offset for database queries. For example, page=2 with limit=20 retrieves questions 21-40.

shopping_mall_buyer_id.description:
Optional filter to retrieve questions from a specific buyer.

When provided, filters the question list to show only questions posted by the buyer with this UUID. Useful for buyer-specific views such as "My Questions" pages or admin interfaces reviewing a specific buyer's activity.

When null or omitted, returns questions from all buyers for the specified product sale. The filter references the shopping_mall_buyer_id field in the shopping_mall_sale_questions table.

has_answer.description:
Optional filter to retrieve questions based on answer status.

When true, returns only questions that have been answered by sellers. When false, returns only unanswered questions awaiting seller response. When null or omitted, returns all questions regardless of answer status.

Sellers use has_answer=false to find pending questions requiring attention. Buyers use has_answer=true to browse already-answered questions for product information.

created_after.description:
Optional filter to retrieve questions created after a specific timestamp.

When provided, returns only questions with created_at >= this ISO 8601 datetime value. Useful for finding recent questions, implementing "What's New" features, or filtering by time period.

Format follows ISO 8601 standard (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ). When null or omitted, no lower bound filter is applied.

created_before.description:
Optional filter to retrieve questions created before a specific timestamp.

When provided, returns only questions with created_at < this ISO 8601 datetime value. Combined with created_after enables date range filtering for historical question analysis or time-bounded reporting.

Format follows ISO 8601 standard (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ). When null or omitted, no upper bound filter is applied.

search.description:
Optional full-text search query for question title and body content.

When provided, performs text search across question titles and body content to find questions matching the search terms. Uses the GIN indexes on title and body fields defined in the Prisma schema for efficient full-text search.

Supports finding questions by keywords, phrases, or specific product features mentioned in questions. When null or omitted, no text filtering is applied. Search is case-insensitive and may support partial word matching depending on database configuration.

oneOf.description: Sort questions by creation timestamp
Sort questions by last modification timestamp

sort.description:
Optional field name to sort question results by.

Specifies which field to use for ordering the question list. Supported values: created_at (default, chronological order), updated_at (recently modified first).

When null or omitted, defaults to created_at ordering. Combined with the order parameter to control ascending vs descending sort direction.

oneOf.description: Ascending order (oldest first for timestamps)
Descending order (newest first for timestamps)

order.description:
Optional sort direction for ordering results.

Specifies whether to sort in ascending (asc) or descending (desc) order. For created_at sorting, desc shows newest questions first (typical default), while asc shows oldest first.

When null or omitted, defaults to desc (newest first) for timestamp-based sorting. This ensures users see the most recent questions by default, which is the expected behavior in Q&A interfaces.

IShoppingMallSaleQuestion.IRequest.description:
Query parameters for searching, filtering, and paginating product sale questions.

Defines the request structure for retrieving filtered lists of customer questions about a product sale. Supports pagination for efficient data loading, filtering by buyer and answer status, date range selection, full-text search, and flexible sorting options.

This request DTO enables multiple use cases including seller dashboards (filtering unanswered questions), buyer research interfaces (searching answered questions), admin moderation tools (filtering by buyer or date range), and general product Q&A browsing with customizable sort orders.

Pagination parameters (limit and page) are required to enforce efficient data retrieval and prevent large uncontrolled result sets. All filter parameters are optional, allowing callers to apply filters as needed while defaulting to showing all questions when no filters are specified.

The search parameter leverages the GIN indexes on title and body fields defined in the shopping_mall_sale_questions Prisma schema, enabling performant full-text search across question content. Date range filtering supports analytics and historical data review workflows.

Used in PATCH /sales/{saleCode}/questions operations to retrieve paginated, filtered question lists with flexible search and sorting capabilities.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the customer question.

This UUID uniquely identifies each question record in the shopping_mall_sale_questions table. Used for referencing specific questions in navigation, APIs, and database relationships.

The ID is automatically generated by the system upon question creation and remains immutable throughout the question lifecycle.

title.description:
Question title or subject summarizing the inquiry.

Brief summary of the question topic that helps buyers and sellers quickly identify the question's focus without reading the full body content. Limited to maximum 200 characters for concise display in list views.

Well-crafted titles improve Q&A browsing experience and help users find relevant questions quickly. They also reduce duplicate questions by making existing inquiries more discoverable.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the question was originally posted by the buyer.

Records the exact date and time when the buyer submitted their question. Automatically set by the system upon question creation and remains immutable.

Supports chronological ordering of questions in list displays and helps buyers assess question recency. Format follows ISO 8601 standard (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ).

buyer.description:
Summary information about the buyer who posted this question.

Provides essential buyer context including name and account identification for attribution purposes. Displaying buyer information in question lists helps sellers prioritize responses and understand their customer base.

The summary representation contains key buyer attributes without exposing sensitive personal information, maintaining appropriate privacy boundaries in public Q&A displays.

has_answer.description:
Indicates whether a seller has provided an answer to this question.

Computed boolean flag derived from the existence of a related record in the shopping_mall_sale_question_answers table. True when an answer exists, false when the question remains unanswered.

Helps buyers quickly identify which questions have been addressed by sellers when browsing Q&A sections. Also enables filtering to show only unanswered questions requiring seller attention or only answered questions for information gathering.

IShoppingMallSaleQuestion.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary representation of customer product questions for list views and paginated displays.

Provides essential question information optimized for performance in question list contexts, search results, and Q&A browsing interfaces. Includes key identification, content preview, timing, and answer status without the full question body or detailed metadata.

This summary variant is used when displaying multiple questions in list format, enabling efficient rendering without loading complete question content. The has_answer field allows users to quickly identify which questions have seller responses, supporting both buyer research workflows and seller response management.

Excludes the full question body to reduce payload size in list operations. Buyers can access complete question details including the full body content and any seller answer by fetching the individual question via the detail endpoint.

Optimized for use in paginated question lists (PATCH /sales/{saleCode}/questions), seller dashboards showing pending questions, and buyer interfaces for browsing product Q&A sections. The minimal field set ensures fast load times while providing sufficient context for navigation and filtering decisions.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the customer question.

This UUID uniquely identifies each question record in the shopping_mall_sale_questions table. The ID is automatically generated by the system upon question creation and remains immutable. It serves as the primary key for referencing specific questions in database relationships and API operations.

shopping_mall_sale_id.description:
Foreign key reference to the parent product sale.

This field establishes the relationship between the question and the specific product sale it concerns. It references the id field in the shopping_mall_sales table, enabling queries to retrieve all questions for a particular product. This foreign key constraint ensures data integrity and prevents orphaned question records.

shopping_mall_buyer_id.description:
Foreign key reference to the buyer who posted the question.

This field identifies which buyer authored this question, referencing the id field in the shopping_mall_buyers table. It enables tracking of buyer engagement and question history, and supports user-specific queries such as retrieving all questions a buyer has asked across the platform.

shopping_mall_buyer_session_id.description:
Session identifier through which the question was submitted.

This field references the specific buyer authentication session used when posting the question, linking to the shopping_mall_buyer_sessions table. It provides audit trail capabilities by tracking which session was active during question submission.

This information is crucial for security monitoring, fraud detection, and compliance purposes. It enables administrators to trace question submissions back to specific login sessions, helping identify suspicious patterns or unauthorized access. The session context also supports debugging and customer support by providing complete interaction history.

title.description:
Question title or subject summarizing the inquiry.

This field contains a brief, concise summary of the question that helps buyers and sellers quickly identify the topic without reading the full question body. The title should be descriptive enough to understand the question's focus at a glance.

Titles are limited to a maximum of 200 characters to ensure they remain concise and scannable in list views. Well-crafted titles improve the browsing experience by allowing users to quickly find relevant questions and answers. They also help avoid duplicate questions by making existing inquiries more discoverable.

body.description:
Detailed question content with buyer's specific inquiry.

This field contains the complete inquiry submitted by the buyer seeking additional information about the product sale. Questions typically concern product features, specifications, availability, shipping, compatibility, or other purchase-related concerns. The body supports multi-line text to accommodate detailed questions with multiple parts.

The content must be between 10 and 2000 characters in length, ensuring questions are substantive enough to be meaningful while preventing excessively long submissions. Questions should be clear, specific, and respectful to enable sellers to provide helpful, accurate responses. Well-formulated questions benefit all potential buyers by building a comprehensive knowledge base about the product.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the question was originally posted.

This field records the exact date and time when the buyer submitted their question. The timestamp is automatically set by the system upon question creation and remains immutable. It helps buyers and sellers understand the recency of questions and supports chronological ordering of Q&A interactions. The format follows ISO 8601 standard (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ).

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the question was last modified.

This field records the most recent modification time for the question content. It is automatically updated by the system whenever the question title or body is edited. The timestamp helps track question editing history and displays to users when questions have been recently updated.

The updated_at field is distinct from created_at, allowing the system to differentiate between original posting time and subsequent modifications. This supports transparency in the Q&A system by showing when questions have been edited after initial submission. The format follows ISO 8601 standard (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ).

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the question.

When this field is set to a timestamp value, the question is considered logically deleted and hidden from public display. However, the question record and all associated data remain in the database to preserve audit trails and maintain data integrity for historical orders or references.

Soft deletion allows administrators to remove inappropriate or policy-violating questions without losing the complete interaction history. Questions can potentially be restored by clearing this field if deletion was performed in error. When null, the question is active and publicly visible. The timestamp format follows ISO 8601 standard (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ).

sale.description:
Summary information about the product sale that this question concerns.

This reference provides essential product context including the sale name, price, and seller information. By including this summary, API consumers can display product details alongside the question without requiring additional API calls. The summary representation contains key fields needed to understand what product is being asked about.

buyer.description:
Summary information about the buyer who posted this question.

This reference includes essential buyer details such as name and account status. Displaying buyer information helps sellers understand who is asking and may influence the nature of their response. The summary provides key buyer attributes without exposing sensitive personal information.

answer.description:
The seller's answer to this question, if one has been provided.

This field contains the complete answer entity when a seller has responded to the question. It includes the answer content, seller information, and timestamps. If no answer has been posted yet, this field is null, indicating an unanswered question that awaits seller response. The one-to-one relationship ensures each question has at most one official seller answer.

IShoppingMallSaleQuestion.description:
Complete representation of a customer question about a product sale.

This entity represents a buyer's inquiry posted on a product listing, seeking additional information before making a purchase decision. Questions enable transparent communication between potential buyers and sellers, helping customers understand product details, features, availability, and other purchase-related concerns. The Q&A system supports informed decision-making and can reduce purchase hesitation.

Each question is associated with a specific product sale and authored by an authenticated buyer. The question may have at most one seller answer, establishing a one-to-one relationship that provides clear, authoritative responses from the product owner. Unanswered questions are visible to sellers, prompting timely responses that demonstrate engagement and customer service quality.

Visibility of questions and answers is public to all users viewing the product, supporting marketplace transparency. This allows potential buyers to benefit from questions asked by others, reducing duplicate inquiries and providing comprehensive product information. The system tracks creation timestamps to support chronological ordering and display question recency.

Security considerations include buyer authentication to prevent spam questions and ensure accountability. The system may implement rate limiting to prevent abuse. Questions are permanently associated with the buyer who posted them, supporting moderation and quality enforcement.

This entity maps to the shopping_mall_sale_questions table in the Prisma database schema. It maintains foreign key relationships with shopping_mall_sales (parent product) and shopping_mall_buyers (question author). The entity supports CRUD operations through dedicated API endpoints, with sellers able to answer questions via related answer endpoints.

IShoppingMallSaleQuestion.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new customer question about a product sale.

Contains the question content submitted by an authenticated buyer seeking additional product information. The buyer's identity is automatically extracted from the JWT authentication token and should not be included in the request body.

This DTO enables buyers to submit questions to sellers, facilitating informed purchase decisions through direct communication. The question will be associated with the product sale specified in the URL path parameter.

title.description:
Question title or subject line.

Brief summary of the question topic (1-200 characters) that helps buyers and sellers quickly identify the question's focus. Should be concise and descriptive to facilitate question browsing.

Example: "What is the battery life?", "Does this come in other colors?", "Is this compatible with Mac?"

body.description:
Full question content submitted by the buyer.

Detailed inquiry text (10-2000 characters) containing the buyer's specific questions or information requests about the product. This is the main body of the question that the seller will respond to.

The minimum length of 10 characters ensures questions are substantive enough to be meaningful. Questions should be clear, specific, and respectful. Avoid including personal contact information or requests for off-platform transactions.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the question answer record.

This UUID serves as the primary key for the answer in the shopping_mall_sale_question_answers table. It is automatically generated by the system when the answer is created and remains immutable throughout the answer's lifetime.

title.description:
Answer title or summary providing a brief overview of the seller's response.

This field contains a concise summary of the answer content, limited to a maximum of 200 characters. The title helps users quickly understand the nature of the seller's response when browsing multiple questions and answers. It should be clear and informative, providing context for the more detailed body content.

The title is displayed prominently in Q&A listings and serves as a quick reference point for both buyers reviewing product information and sellers managing their customer engagement. A well-crafted title improves the discoverability and usefulness of the answer.

body.description:
Detailed answer content addressing the buyer's question with comprehensive information.

This field contains the complete response text provided by the seller, with a minimum length of 10 characters and maximum of 2000 characters. The body should thoroughly address the customer's inquiry about the product, providing clear, helpful, and accurate information to assist potential buyers in making informed purchase decisions.

The detailed body content is where sellers can elaborate on product features, specifications, availability, shipping details, or other relevant information requested by the buyer. Answer quality directly impacts buyer confidence and seller reputation, as all potential buyers viewing the product can see these responses.

Sellers should maintain a professional and helpful tone in the body content, as it reflects their customer service quality and commitment to buyer satisfaction.

shopping_mall_seller_id.description:
Foreign key reference to the seller who provided this answer.

This UUID identifies which seller authored the response, referencing the id field in the shopping_mall_sellers table. It establishes ownership of the answer and enables tracking of seller engagement and response patterns across the platform.

The seller_id is automatically populated from the authenticated seller's JWT token during answer creation, ensuring accurate attribution and preventing impersonation. This field supports seller-specific queries such as retrieving all answers a seller has provided, calculating response rates, and assessing seller engagement metrics.

shopping_mall_seller_session_id.description:
Session identifier through which the answer was submitted for comprehensive audit tracking.

This UUID references the specific authentication session in the shopping_mall_seller_sessions table that was active when the seller posted their answer. It provides detailed audit trail capabilities, linking each answer to the exact session context including IP address, user agent, and timestamp information.

Session tracking supports security monitoring, fraud detection, and accountability enforcement. It enables administrators to investigate suspicious activity patterns and maintain comprehensive records of all seller interactions with the platform.

shopping_mall_sale_question_id.description:
Foreign key reference to the parent product question.

This UUID links the answer to the specific customer question it responds to in the shopping_mall_sale_questions table. It establishes the relationship between questions and their corresponding seller answers, maintaining the one-to-one constraint that ensures each question has at most one official seller response.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the seller provided this answer.

This ISO 8601 formatted datetime indicates when the seller originally posted their response to the customer's question. It helps users understand the recency and timeliness of seller responses, which can be an important factor in assessing seller engagement and customer service quality.

The creation timestamp is automatically set by the system when the answer record is first inserted and remains immutable throughout the answer's lifetime. It supports chronological ordering of answers and enables time-based analytics of seller response patterns.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the answer was last modified by the seller.

This ISO 8601 formatted datetime records the most recent update to the answer content, whether title or body. It is automatically refreshed by the system whenever the seller edits their response, providing transparency about answer currency and modification history.

The updated timestamp helps buyers distinguish between original responses and subsequently revised answers. It supports audit trails and enables users to understand whether an answer has been modified since they last viewed it. For newly created answers that have never been edited, this timestamp will match the created_at value.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp indicating when the answer was removed from public display.

When this field is set to a datetime value, the answer is considered deleted and hidden from public view while preserving the complete audit trail and data integrity. Null values indicate the answer is active and publicly visible.

Soft deletion enables content moderation, policy enforcement, and seller-initiated answer removal while maintaining historical records for compliance and analytics purposes. Deleted answers may be recoverable by administrators within a retention period, supporting dispute resolution and mistake correction workflows.

The soft delete pattern preserves referential integrity in the database and prevents cascading data loss that could affect related records or historical transaction data.

IShoppingMallSaleQuestionAnswer.description:
Complete seller answer to a customer product question with full audit trail and content structure.

This schema represents the comprehensive details of a seller's response to a customer inquiry about a product sale. It includes all information stored in the shopping_mall_sale_question_answers table, providing complete transparency about answer content, authorship, timing, and lifecycle status.

Answers are structured with both a brief title for quick scanning and detailed body content for comprehensive responses. This dual-field design supports efficient Q&A browsing while enabling sellers to provide thorough, helpful information that addresses buyer concerns completely.

The schema captures full audit trail information including the seller who authored the response, the session through which it was submitted, and timestamps for creation, modification, and potential deletion. This comprehensive tracking supports accountability, security monitoring, and seller performance analytics.

Answers become immediately visible to all users viewing the product question upon creation, helping potential buyers understand product details and assess seller responsiveness. The presence and quality of seller answers significantly impact buyer confidence and purchase decisions, making this a critical component of the marketplace trust infrastructure.

title.description:
Updated title or summary of the seller's answer to the customer question.

This field contains the revised brief summary of the answer, limited to a maximum of 200 characters. When updating an answer, sellers can refine the title to better represent the content of their response, improve clarity, or correct any inaccuracies in the original summary.

The updated title replaces the previous title text entirely and should remain clear and informative to help users quickly understand the nature of the seller's response. Title updates are immediately visible to all users viewing the product question.

body.description:
Updated detailed content of the seller's answer to the customer question.

This field contains the revised comprehensive response text, with a minimum length of 10 characters and maximum of 2000 characters. When updating an answer, the seller may correct errors, add additional details, or clarify previous statements to better address the customer's inquiry.

The updated body content replaces the previous answer text entirely. Answer quality should remain helpful, accurate, and professional, as all potential buyers viewing the product will see this updated response. The body is where sellers provide the substantive information that helps buyers make informed purchase decisions.

IShoppingMallSaleQuestionAnswer.IUpdate.description:
Request payload for updating an existing seller answer to a customer product question with complete content structure.

This DTO represents the data required when a seller modifies their response to a customer inquiry. The update operation allows sellers to improve answer quality, correct mistakes, add additional information, or refine both the summary title and detailed body content to better serve potential buyers.

Both fields are optional for update operations, enabling partial updates where sellers can modify just the title, just the body, or both fields simultaneously. This flexibility supports efficient answer refinement without requiring clients to resend unchanged content. Backend validation ensures that if provided, each field meets its constraints (title maximum 200 characters, body between 10-2000 characters).

Only the answer content (title and body) can be modified through this update operation. The answer's relationship to the question, the seller who authored it, and the original creation timestamp remain immutable to preserve data integrity and maintain accurate attribution of responses. The updated_at timestamp is automatically refreshed by the system upon each modification.

Security considerations include ownership verification to ensure that only the seller who originally created the answer can modify it. The system prevents unauthorized users from editing answers that don't belong to them. This validation occurs at the API layer by comparing the authenticated seller's ID from the JWT token against the answer's seller ownership.

This DTO is used in PUT operations for answer modification endpoints. The operation validates that both the question and the existing answer belong to the specified sale and seller before allowing the update. Updated answers are immediately visible to all users viewing the product question, ensuring customers always see the most current and accurate seller information.

title.description:
Brief summary or title of the seller's answer to the customer's product question.

This field provides a concise headline for the answer, making it easier for users to quickly scan and understand the topic of the response. The title should capture the essence of the answer in a clear and informative manner.

The title is limited to 200 characters maximum as defined in the shopping_mall_sale_question_answers Prisma schema. It serves as a quick reference point in answer listings and helps organize multiple answers when browsing product Q&A sections.

This field is required and must be provided when creating a new answer. It complements the detailed body content by giving users an at-a-glance understanding of what the answer addresses.

body.description:
Detailed answer content provided by the seller addressing the customer's product inquiry.

This field contains the comprehensive response text that thoroughly addresses the customer's question about the product. The content should be clear, helpful, accurate, and professional to assist potential buyers in making informed purchase decisions and to build trust in the seller's expertise and responsiveness.

The body must be between 10 and 2000 characters as enforced by the shopping_mall_sale_question_answers Prisma schema constraints. This ensures answers are substantive enough to be helpful (minimum 10 characters) while remaining concise and readable (maximum 2000 characters).

The answer body becomes immediately visible to all users viewing the product question once created. High-quality, detailed answers can significantly impact buyer confidence and purchase decisions by demonstrating the seller's knowledge and commitment to customer service.

IShoppingMallSaleQuestionAnswer.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a seller's answer to a customer product question.

This schema represents the data required when a seller responds to a customer's inquiry about their product listing. It includes both a brief title summarizing the answer and a detailed body providing the comprehensive response.

The seller's identity is automatically extracted from the JWT authentication token, ensuring that only the actual seller of the product can create answers. The operation validates that the question exists and belongs to the specified sale before creating the answer.

Security measures prevent unauthorized users from posting answers on behalf of sellers. The system enforces character length constraints to ensure answers are both substantive and concise, maintaining quality standards across the marketplace.

This DTO maps to the shopping_mall_sale_question_answers table in the Prisma schema, creating a new answer record with title and body fields linked to a specific question on a product sale.

shopping_mall_sale_id.description:
Filter snapshots by specific product sale.

When provided, returns only snapshots associated with the specified sale ID. Useful for retrieving complete snapshot history for a single product.

When null or omitted, returns snapshots across all sales (subject to authorization constraints).

status.description:
Filter snapshots by product status at snapshot time.

Valid values: draft, pending_approval, published, suspended, archived. Returns snapshots where the product had the specified status when captured.

Useful for analyzing product lifecycle transitions or finding snapshots from specific product states.

When null or omitted, returns snapshots regardless of status.

created_at_from.description:
Filter snapshots created on or after this timestamp.

Enables temporal range queries for snapshot history. Combined with created_at_to, allows filtering snapshots within specific time periods.

When null or omitted, no lower bound is applied to snapshot creation time.

created_at_to.description:
Filter snapshots created on or before this timestamp.

Enables temporal range queries for snapshot history. Combined with created_at_from, allows filtering snapshots within specific time periods.

When null or omitted, no upper bound is applied to snapshot creation time.

limit.description:
Maximum number of snapshot records to return per page.

Controls pagination size for snapshot history queries. Must be between 1 and 100.

When null or omitted, uses platform default pagination size (typically 20).

page.description:
Page number for pagination, starting from 1.

Enables navigation through large snapshot history sets. Combined with limit to implement offset-based pagination.

When null or omitted, defaults to page 1.

oneOf.description: Sort snapshots by creation timestamp in ascending order (oldest first).
Sort snapshots by creation timestamp in descending order (newest first).

sort.description:
Sort order for snapshot results.

Valid values: created_at (ascending chronological order), -created_at (descending chronological order).

When null or omitted, defaults to descending chronological order (newest snapshots first) for typical audit trail usage.

IShoppingMallSaleSnapshot.IRequest.description:
Query parameters for searching and filtering product sale snapshots.

Enables retrieval of historical snapshot records with flexible filtering by sale, status, temporal range, and pagination controls. Used in snapshot history operations to access audit trails and track product evolution over time.

Supports filtering snapshots by specific product (shopping_mall_sale_id), product status at snapshot time, and temporal range (created_at_from/created_at_to). Pagination parameters (limit, page) control result set size for managing large snapshot histories.

Sort parameter allows chronological ordering of snapshots, with descending order (newest first) as the default to prioritize recent product states. This request DTO is typically used in PATCH /sales/{saleCode}/snapshots operations for comprehensive snapshot history queries.

All filter parameters are optional, allowing flexible query construction from broad snapshot lists to highly specific historical lookups.

id.description: Primary key uniquely identifying this sale snapshot record.

shopping_mall_sale_id.description: Reference to the base product sale entity that this snapshot captures.

title.description: Product title at snapshot time for display in lists.

code.description: Product code at snapshot time for identification.

status.description: Product status at snapshot time. Values: draft, pending_approval, published, suspended, archived.

created_at.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was created.

IShoppingMallSaleSnapshot.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary of sale snapshot for list displays and references.

Provides essential snapshot identification and temporal information without the complete denormalized product data.
Used in snapshot history lists and timeline displays.

id.description:
Primary key uniquely identifying this sale snapshot record.

Each snapshot has a unique UUID that serves as the immutable identifier for this historical point-in-time capture of product sale information.

shopping_mall_sale_id.description:
Reference to the base product sale entity that this snapshot captures.

Links to the main sales record in the shopping_mall_sales table, establishing the relationship between historical snapshots and current product data.

sale.description:
Base product sale entity that this snapshot references.

Provides context about the product being tracked through snapshots, enabling navigation from historical data to current product state.

shopping_mall_seller_id.description:
Seller who owned the product at the time this snapshot was created.

Denormalized seller reference preserving historical ownership even if product ownership changes in the future.

seller.description:
Seller account information at snapshot time.

Provides seller context for historical product data, enabling audit trails and ownership verification for historical transactions.

shopping_mall_category_id.description:
Category assignment at the time this snapshot was created.

Denormalized category reference preserving historical categorization even if product is recategorized later.

category.description:
Category information at snapshot time.

Provides category context for historical product organization, preserving how the product was classified when this snapshot was captured.

code.description:
Product code at snapshot time, denormalized for historical accuracy.

Captures the product's business identifier as it existed at this point in time, preserving historical SKU tracking even if codes change.

title.description:
Product title at snapshot time, denormalized to preserve historical product naming.

Stores the exact product name as displayed to buyers when this snapshot was created, maintaining accuracy for historical orders and references.

description.description:
Product description at snapshot time, denormalized to preserve historical product details.

Captures the complete product description text as it existed at this moment, ensuring orders reference accurate product information from purchase time.

brand.description:
Brand name at snapshot time, denormalized for historical preservation.

Records the product brand as it was listed when this snapshot was captured, maintaining brand information consistency for historical analysis.

This field is optional and may be null if brand information was not specified at snapshot time.

condition.description:
Product condition at snapshot time.

Valid values: new, refurbished, used. Preserves the condition classification as it existed at snapshot creation time.

status.description:
Product status at snapshot time.

Valid values: draft, pending_approval, published, suspended, archived. Captures the product's lifecycle state when this snapshot was created.

short_description.description:
Short description at snapshot time, denormalized for historical accuracy.

Preserves the brief product summary as it appeared in listing displays when this snapshot was captured.

This field is optional and may be null if a short description was not provided at snapshot time.

meta_keywords.description:
SEO keywords at snapshot time, denormalized for historical preservation.

Records the search optimization keywords as configured when this snapshot was created.

This field is optional and may be null if SEO keywords were not specified at snapshot time.

weight.description:
Product weight at snapshot time in kilograms, denormalized for shipping calculation history.

Preserves the weight value used for shipping cost calculations at the time of this snapshot.

This field is optional and may be null if weight was not specified at snapshot time.

dimension_length.description:
Length dimension at snapshot time in centimeters.

Captures the product length as specified when this snapshot was created, maintaining dimensional accuracy for historical shipping calculations.

This field is optional and may be null if length dimension was not specified at snapshot time.

dimension_width.description:
Width dimension at snapshot time in centimeters.

Records the product width as it existed at snapshot time for historical dimensional reference.

This field is optional and may be null if width dimension was not specified at snapshot time.

dimension_height.description:
Height dimension at snapshot time in centimeters.

Preserves the product height measurement from the time this snapshot was captured.

This field is optional and may be null if height dimension was not specified at snapshot time.

manufacturer.description:
Manufacturer name at snapshot time, denormalized for historical accuracy.

Stores the manufacturer information as listed when this snapshot was created.

This field is optional and may be null if manufacturer information was not specified at snapshot time.

return_policy_days.description:
Return policy at snapshot time, measured in number of days.

Valid values: 0, 7, 14, 30, or 60. Preserves the return window that was applicable when this snapshot was captured, ensuring historical order return policies remain accurate.

warranty_info.description:
Warranty information at snapshot time, denormalized for historical preservation.

Captures warranty details and duration as they were specified when this snapshot was created.

This field is optional and may be null if warranty information was not specified at snapshot time.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this snapshot was created, representing the exact point-in-time captured.

Marks the moment this historical record was generated, serving as the temporal anchor for all denormalized data in this snapshot.

IShoppingMallSaleSnapshot.description:
Historical point-in-time captures of product sale information for audit trails and version control.

Stores complete product state at specific moments to preserve historical data accuracy.
Snapshots are created when significant product changes occur, enabling tracking of price changes, description modifications, and product evolution over time.

Each snapshot denormalizes product information from the main sale entity to maintain historical accuracy even if current product data changes.
This ensures orders reference the product information as it existed at purchase time.

Snapshots are append-only with no updates after creation.
Used for compliance, dispute resolution, and historical reporting.

total_quantity.description:
Initial total inventory quantity to set for this SKU variant.

Represents the starting inventory level when first establishing inventory tracking for a product variant. This value corresponds to the total_quantity field in the shopping_mall_inventory_stocks table and reflects the actual physical stock available at the time of creation.

Must be a non-negative integer representing countable inventory units. When creating inventory stock, the system automatically initializes reserved_quantity to 0 and calculates available_quantity as equal to this total_quantity value.

This field maps directly to the Prisma schema's total_quantity column, which stores the complete stock level before accounting for reservations.

low_stock_threshold.description:
Seller-configured threshold triggering low stock alerts.

Defines the inventory level at or below which the system notifies sellers to restock this SKU variant. This corresponds to the low_stock_threshold field in the shopping_mall_inventory_stocks table.

When the available_quantity falls to or below this threshold, automated alerts are sent to sellers prompting them to replenish inventory. This helps prevent stockouts and ensures continuous product availability.

Must be a non-negative integer. If not provided during creation, the system applies a default value of 10 units as specified in the Prisma schema. Sellers can customize this based on product characteristics, sales velocity, and restocking lead times.

IShoppingMallInventoryStock.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating initial inventory stock tracking for a product SKU variant.

Contains the minimal information required to establish inventory tracking for a new product SKU. When creating inventory stock, the system automatically initializes reserved_quantity to 0 and calculates available_quantity as equal to the provided total_quantity.

The saleSkuId is provided via the URL path parameter rather than in the request body, ensuring the inventory stock is correctly associated with the target product variant. The low_stock_threshold can optionally be configured during creation, otherwise defaulting to 10 units.

Security: Only sellers who own the parent product sale can create inventory stock for its SKUs. The system validates ownership before allowing creation.

total_quantity.description:
Updated total inventory quantity for this SKU variant.

Represents the new absolute inventory level after restocking, corrections, or adjustments. This field corresponds to the total_quantity column in the shopping_mall_inventory_stocks table.

The system validates that this value is not less than the currently reserved_quantity to prevent overselling. Must be a non-negative integer representing the complete stock level.

When updated, the available_quantity is automatically recalculated as (total_quantity - reserved_quantity), ensuring accurate real-time inventory visibility for buyers and the checkout process.

low_stock_threshold.description:
Updated low stock alert threshold for this SKU variant.

Allows sellers to modify the inventory level at or below which low stock alerts are triggered. This corresponds to the low_stock_threshold field in the shopping_mall_inventory_stocks table.

Sellers may need to adjust this threshold based on changing business conditions such as seasonal demand patterns, supply chain improvements reducing lead times, or product lifecycle changes.

Must be a non-negative integer. Updates to this field immediately affect future low stock alert triggers, helping sellers maintain optimal inventory levels adapted to current business requirements.

IShoppingMallInventoryStock.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating inventory stock information for a product SKU variant.

Contains fields that can be modified after initial inventory stock creation. All fields are optional, allowing partial updates to either total_quantity, low_stock_threshold, or both.

The update operation maintains data integrity by validating that new total_quantity values don't conflict with existing reserved_quantity amounts. The saleSkuId is provided via the URL path parameter to identify which inventory stock record to update.

Changes are logged in the inventory transaction history for complete audit traceability. Security: Only sellers who own the parent product sale can update inventory stock for its SKUs. The system validates ownership and enforces business rules around minimum stock levels and reserved quantity constraints.

id.description:
Primary key uniquely identifying this inventory transaction record.

Each transaction has a unique UUID serving as the immutable identifier for this inventory movement in the audit trail.

shopping_mall_sale_sku_id.description:
Product SKU variant affected by this inventory transaction.

Links to the specific product variant whose inventory quantity was changed by this transaction.

sku.description:
Product SKU variant information for this transaction.

Provides context about which product variant's inventory was affected, enabling detailed inventory movement tracking.

shopping_mall_order_id.description:
Related order that triggered this inventory transaction.

Nullable for non-order transactions like manual adjustments. Links inventory changes to specific customer orders when applicable.

order.description:
Order information that triggered this transaction.

Provides order context for inventory changes resulting from sales, cancellations, or returns. Null for manual adjustments.

shopping_mall_seller_id.description:
Seller who owns the SKU and triggered manual inventory changes.

Nullable for system-triggered transactions. Links manual adjustments to the seller who performed them.

seller.description:
Seller account information for manual transactions.

Provides seller context for inventory adjustments, enabling accountability and audit trails. Null for automated system transactions.

transaction_type.description:
Type of inventory transaction indicating the nature of the inventory change.

Valid values: addition (new stock received), reduction (damaged goods removed), sale (order placed deducting inventory), cancellation (order cancelled restoring stock), return (refunded product restocked), adjustment (manual correction), reconciliation (system correction).

Determines whether the quantity change increases or decreases inventory and provides context for the movement.

quantity_change.description:
Quantity change amount representing the delta applied to inventory.

Positive values for additions, returns, and cancellations that increase inventory. Negative values for sales and reductions that decrease inventory. Zero not allowed. Represents the exact units added or removed.

previous_quantity.description:
Inventory total quantity before this transaction was applied.

Captured for audit trail and reconciliation purposes, enabling verification that the transaction calculation was correct.

new_quantity.description:
Inventory total quantity after this transaction was applied.

Should equal previous_quantity plus quantity_change. Captured for validation and audit, enabling detection of calculation errors.

reason.description:
Explanation or reason for this inventory transaction.

Required for manual adjustments and reductions to document why inventory was changed. Optional for automated system transactions. Maximum 500 characters.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this inventory transaction occurred.

Immutable once recorded for audit integrity. Marks the exact moment the inventory change was processed.

IShoppingMallInventoryTransaction.description:
Historical audit trail of all inventory quantity changes and movements.

Records every inventory operation including seller manual adjustments, automated sales deductions, order cancellations restoring stock, returns adding inventory back, and system reconciliation corrections.

Each transaction captures the before and after quantities, the change amount, the transaction type, and the reason or context for the change. This provides complete traceability for inventory discrepancies, financial auditing, and seller analytics.

Transaction types include addition (new stock received), reduction (damaged goods removed), sale (order placed), cancellation (order cancelled restoring stock), return (refunded product restocked), adjustment (manual correction), and reconciliation (system correction).

This table enables sellers to review inventory movement history, investigate discrepancies, and analyze stock performance. It supports daily reconciliation processes that detect and correct data inconsistencies.

Transactions are immutable once recorded, creating a permanent audit trail. The related order identifier links inventory changes to specific orders when applicable. Seller or system identifiers track who or what triggered each transaction.

id.description: Primary key uniquely identifying this inventory transaction.

shopping_mall_sale_sku_id.description: Product SKU variant affected by this transaction.

transaction_type.description: Type of inventory transaction. Values: addition, reduction, sale, cancellation, return, adjustment, reconciliation.

quantity_change.description: Quantity change amount. Positive for increases, negative for decreases.

created_at.description: Timestamp when this transaction occurred.

IShoppingMallInventoryTransaction.ISumma.description:
Lightweight summary of inventory transaction for list displays and audit trails.

Provides essential transaction details including type, quantity change, and timing without complete contextual information.
Used in inventory movement history lists and reconciliation reports.

page.description:
Page number for pagination, starting from 1.

Specifies which page of results to retrieve when the total number of transactions exceeds the page size limit. Used in conjunction with limit to implement cursor-based pagination for efficient navigation through large transaction histories.

limit.description:
Maximum number of transaction records to return per page.

Controls the page size for pagination, with a reasonable maximum to ensure optimal performance. Smaller limits provide faster response times, while larger limits reduce the number of requests needed to retrieve complete datasets.

shopping_mall_sale_sku_id.description:
Optional filter to retrieve transactions for a specific product SKU variant.

When provided, restricts results to only those transactions affecting the specified SKU. This enables focused analysis of inventory movements for individual product variants, supporting SKU-level reconciliation and auditing.

transaction_type.description:
Optional filter to retrieve transactions of a specific type.

When provided, restricts results to transactions matching the specified type such as 'purchase', 'sale', 'adjustment', 'reservation', or 'release'. This enables analysis of specific inventory movement patterns and operational activities.

from_date.description:
Optional start date for filtering transactions by creation timestamp.

When provided, returns only transactions created on or after this date. Used in conjunction with to_date to define a specific time range for inventory analysis, reporting, and reconciliation within specific periods.

to_date.description:
Optional end date for filtering transactions by creation timestamp.

When provided, returns only transactions created on or before this date. Used in conjunction with from_date to define a specific time range for inventory analysis, reporting, and reconciliation within specific periods.

Field to use for sorting the transaction results.

Determines the primary ordering of returned transactions. 'created_at' sorts by timestamp (useful for chronological audit trails), while 'quantity_change' sorts by the magnitude of inventory impact (useful for identifying significant movements).
