Buyers can save multiple payment methods and designate one as their default for convenient checkout.
Payment methods support soft deletion to maintain audit trails while allowing buyers to remove unused methods from their active list.

The system stores only payment provider tokens and last four digits for identification - never full card numbers or CVV codes.
All payment methods must be verified through the payment provider before being marked as usable for transactions.

payment_type.description:
Type of payment method being registered.

Specifies the category of payment instrument, such as 'credit_card', 'debit_card', 'digital_wallet', or other supported payment types. This field determines which validation rules and processing logic the system applies. Different payment types may require different sets of additional fields and follow different security protocols.

provider.description:
Payment provider or payment gateway name.

Identifies the third-party payment processor handling this payment method, such as 'Stripe', 'PayPal', 'Square', 'Braintree', or other integrated payment providers. The provider must be one of the supported payment gateways configured in the platform. This field determines which provider API will be used for payment processing.

provider_token.description:
Tokenized payment method identifier obtained from the payment provider.

This secure token must be obtained from the payment gateway (Stripe, PayPal, etc.) before submitting this registration request. The token represents the actual payment instrument and is used instead of transmitting raw payment details for PCI DSS compliance. Clients typically obtain this token through the payment provider's client-side SDK or tokenization API.

card_brand.description:
Brand of the credit or debit card.

Indicates the card network or issuer brand such as 'Visa', 'Mastercard', 'American Express', 'Discover', 'JCB', etc. This field is required when payment_type is 'credit_card' or 'debit_card'. The card brand is used for display purposes and applying brand-specific validation rules.

Null for non-card payment methods like PayPal or bank transfers.

last_four_digits.description:
Last four digits of the card number or account identifier.

For security purposes, only the last four digits of the card number should be provided. This allows buyers to identify their cards without exposing the full card number. The full card number should never be transmitted to the backend - instead, use the payment provider's tokenization mechanism.

Null for payment methods that don't have a meaningful digit-based identifier.

expiry_month.description:
Card expiration month (1-12) if the payment type is a card.

The month component of the card's expiration date, represented as an integer from 1 to 12 (1 = January, 12 = December). This field is required when payment_type is 'credit_card' or 'debit_card'. The system validates that the card has not expired based on this value and expiry_year.

Used in combination with expiry_year to validate card is not expired before processing payments. Platform can warn buyers proactively when cards are approaching expiration. Null for non-card payment methods.

expiry_year.description:
Card expiration year (four-digit format) if the payment type is a card.

The year component of the card's expiration date, represented as a four-digit integer (e.g., 2025, 2026). This field is required when payment_type is 'credit_card' or 'debit_card'. The system validates that the combination of expiry_month and expiry_year represents a future date.

Stored as full year value for unambiguous expiration validation. Used in combination with expiry_month to prevent processing with expired cards. Null for non-card payment methods.

billing_name.description:
Cardholder name or billing name for the payment method.

The full name of the person or entity to whom the payment method is issued, exactly as it appears on the card or in the payment account. This name is used for verification purposes during payment processing and should match the payment provider's records.

Typically matches the cardholder name or account holder name. Required for all payment method types to ensure proper payment attribution.

billing_postal_code.description:
Postal code of the billing address.

The ZIP or postal code associated with the billing address for this payment method. This field is used for Address Verification Service (AVS) checks during payment processing to reduce fraud risk. The postal code should match the billing address on file with the card issuer or payment provider.

Helps prevent fraud by validating the buyer has legitimate access to the payment method. Null if the payment provider or payment type doesn't require postal code verification.

is_default.description:
Flag indicating whether this should be set as the buyer's default payment method.

When set to true, this payment method will become the buyer's default payment option, automatically pre-selected during checkout. If another payment method is currently set as default, it will automatically be updated to is_default false. Defaults to false if not specified, meaning the payment method is saved but not set as the default option.

Only one payment method per buyer can be marked as default. Buyers can change their default payment method at any time through account settings.

IShoppingMallPaymentMethod.ICreate.description:
Request body for registering a new payment method to a buyer's account.

This type defines the data structure required to create a new payment method record in the shopping_mall_payment_methods table. It contains the essential information needed to securely save a payment instrument for future use in checkout transactions.

The buyer's identity (shopping_mall_buyer_id) is automatically extracted from the JWT authentication token and must NOT be included in this request body. This ensures secure association of payment methods with the correct buyer account and prevents unauthorized creation of payment methods for other users.

Security considerations are paramount in payment method registration. The provider_token must be obtained from a supported payment provider (Stripe, PayPal, Square, Braintree) before submission - clients should never transmit raw payment card details directly to the backend. Instead, use the payment provider's client-side SDK or tokenization API to securely obtain the provider_token, which serves as a secure reference to the actual payment instrument stored by the provider.

For credit and debit cards, only the last_four_digits should be transmitted (never the full card number), along with the card_brand, expiry_month, and expiry_year. The full card number is handled exclusively by the payment provider's tokenization process. The billing_name and billing_postal_code are used for Address Verification Service (AVS) checks during payment processing.

The is_default flag allows buyers to immediately designate this payment method as their preferred default option. If set to true, any previously default payment method for this buyer will automatically be updated to is_default false, maintaining the business rule of exclusive default status.

The is_verified field is set automatically by the system after validating the payment method through the payment provider and is not included in the client request. All required validation, tokenization verification, and security checks are performed by the backend before the payment method is saved. The system ensures PCI DSS compliance through tokenization and never stores raw payment card numbers in the database.

IShoppingMallPaymentMethod.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for modifying existing payment method details.

This schema represents the request body for updating payment method information in a buyer's account. It enables buyers to modify payment method details such as billing address information and default status preferences without needing to delete and re-add the payment method.

All fields are optional to support partial updates, allowing buyers to modify specific fields without affecting other payment method details. Immutable fields like provider_token, card_brand, and card_last_four_digits cannot be updated for security and compliance reasons - buyers must delete and re-add payment methods to change these values.

When is_default is set to true, the system automatically updates other payment methods to is_default false, ensuring only one default payment method exists per buyer account.

billing_name.description:
Name on the billing account or card.

This field represents the cardholder name or account holder name associated with the payment method. It may be updated if the buyer's name changes or if there was an error in the original entry.

The billing name is used for payment verification and must match the name on the payment method as registered with the payment provider.

billing_postal_code.description:
Postal code of the billing address.

This field represents the ZIP code or postal code associated with the payment method's billing address. It is often used for payment verification through Address Verification Service (AVS) checks.

Buyers may update this field if their billing address changes or to correct entry errors.

is_default.description:
Whether this payment method should be the default payment method for the buyer.

When set to true, this payment method becomes the default choice during checkout. The system automatically sets is_default to false for all other payment methods belonging to the buyer, ensuring only one default payment method exists per account.

This field allows buyers to change their preferred payment method without deleting and re-adding payment methods.

IShoppingMallPaymentTransaction.IRequest.description:
Search and filter criteria for payment transaction queries.

This schema defines the request parameters for searching and filtering payment transaction records with pagination support. It enables complex queries based on transaction status, payment method details, buyer information, order references, transaction dates, and payment amounts.

The schema supports comprehensive filtering for various use cases including buyer payment history review, seller revenue tracking, administrator financial auditing, and dispute resolution. All filter criteria are optional, allowing flexible query construction from simple to highly specific searches.

Pagination parameters enable efficient navigation through potentially large transaction datasets, while sorting options allow ordering by transaction date, amount, status, or other relevant fields in ascending or descending order.

page.description:
Page number for pagination (1-based indexing).

This field specifies which page of results to retrieve. Combined with limit, it enables efficient navigation through large transaction datasets without loading all records at once.

Default value is typically 1 if not specified.

limit.description:
Number of transaction records to return per page.

This field controls the page size for pagination. The maximum value is typically enforced to prevent performance issues from excessively large page sizes.

Default value is typically 20-50 records if not specified.

sort_by.description:
Field name to sort results by.

This field specifies which transaction attribute to use for sorting. Common sort fields include 'created_at' (transaction timestamp), 'amount' (payment amount), 'transaction_status' (status), and 'updated_at' (last modification time).

When combined with sort_order, this enables flexible result ordering to meet various display and analysis requirements.

oneOf.description:
Sort direction for ordered results.

This field specifies whether to sort in ascending ('asc') or descending ('desc') order. Combined with sort_by, it controls the order of returned transaction records.

Descending order is commonly used for timestamp fields to show recent transactions first.

Sort direction for ordered results.

This field specifies whether to sort in ascending ('asc') or descending ('desc') order. Combined with sort_by, it controls the order of returned transaction records.

Descending order is commonly used for timestamp fields to show recent transactions first.

sort_order.description:
Sort direction for ordered results.

This field specifies whether to sort in ascending ('asc') or descending ('desc') order. Combined with sort_by, it controls the order of returned transaction records.

Descending order is commonly used for timestamp fields to show recent transactions first.

transaction_status.description:
Filter by payment transaction status.

This field filters transactions based on their processing status such as 'pending', 'completed', 'failed', 'refunded', or 'cancelled'. It enables searching for transactions in specific states for monitoring, reporting, or troubleshooting purposes.

Multiple statuses may be supported through comma-separated values or array format depending on implementation.

payment_method_provider.description:
Filter by payment provider type.

This field filters transactions based on the payment method provider such as 'credit_card', 'paypal', 'bank_transfer', etc. It is useful for analyzing transaction patterns by payment method or generating provider-specific reports.

buyer_id.description:
Filter by buyer who made the payment.

This field filters transactions to show only those belonging to a specific buyer. It is typically used by administrators for buyer-specific financial queries or dispute resolution.

For buyer-scoped operations, this filter may be automatically set to the authenticated buyer's ID from the JWT token.

order_id.description:
Filter by associated order identifier.

This field filters transactions to show only those related to a specific order. It is commonly used when displaying payment history for a particular order or investigating order-specific payment issues.

amount_min.description:
Minimum transaction amount filter (inclusive).

This field sets the lower bound for transaction amount filtering. When specified, only transactions with amounts greater than or equal to this value are returned.

Useful for finding high-value transactions or filtering out small payments in financial analysis.

amount_max.description:
Maximum transaction amount filter (inclusive).

This field sets the upper bound for transaction amount filtering. When specified, only transactions with amounts less than or equal to this value are returned.

Useful for finding transactions within specific amount ranges or identifying suspicious large payments.

created_at_start.description:
Filter transactions created on or after this timestamp.

This field sets the start of the transaction date range filter. When specified, only transactions created on or after this timestamp are returned.

Commonly used for generating financial reports for specific time periods or analyzing transaction trends over time.

created_at_end.description:
Filter transactions created on or before this timestamp.

This field sets the end of the transaction date range filter. When specified, only transactions created on or before this timestamp are returned.

Combined with created_at_start, this enables precise date range filtering for reporting and analysis purposes.

search.description:
General search term for transaction records.

This field enables full-text search across relevant transaction fields such as transaction ID, gateway reference numbers, or buyer information. It provides a user-friendly way to find specific transactions without knowing exact field values.

The implementation may search across multiple fields and support partial matching for improved discoverability.

id.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for the payment transaction.

oneOf.description: Type of transaction. Authorization holds funds, capture completes payment.

IShoppingMallPaymentTransaction.ISummary.description:
Lightweight payment transaction summary for references.

Provides essential payment transaction information for use in other entities.
Used when refund transactions reference the original payment being refunded.

Includes key identifiers, amounts, and status without detailed provider responses.

payment_method_id.description:
Identifier of the payment method to use for this transaction.

References a saved payment method from the shopping_mall_payment_methods table that belongs to the authenticated buyer. The payment method must be active and valid when provided. This could be a saved credit card token, bank account reference, or digital wallet identifier.

This field is optional (nullable) to support scenarios where buyers enter payment details directly at checkout without using a saved payment method. When null, the buyer provides payment information inline during the transaction creation process, and the payment gateway tokenizes it directly.

When provided, the system validates that the specified payment method belongs to the authenticated buyer and is verified for use. Corresponds to the shopping_mall_payment_method_id column in the Prisma schema.

oneOf.description: Type of transaction indicating the operation being performed. Authorization holds funds on the payment method without completing the transfer.
Type of transaction indicating the operation being performed. Capture completes the payment transfer after a successful authorization.
Type of transaction indicating the operation being performed. Void cancels a previous authorization before capture.
Type of transaction indicating the operation being performed. Refund returns captured funds to the buyer.

transaction_type.description:
Type of payment transaction indicating the operation being performed.

Valid values: authorization, capture, void, refund. Authorization holds funds on the payment method, capture completes the payment transfer. Void cancels an authorization, refund returns captured funds to the buyer. Determines the financial effect and reversibility of the transaction.

For order payments, the typical flow is authorization followed by capture. The authorization verifies funds availability and holds the amount, while capture finalizes the transfer when the order is ready to ship.

amount.description:
Transaction amount to process.

The payment amount for this transaction, which must match the order total to prevent payment manipulation. This amount includes all order costs: item subtotals, taxes, shipping fees, and any applicable discounts. The system validates this amount against the associated order's total before initiating payment processing.

currency.description:
Currency code for the payment amount.

ISO 4217 three-letter currency code (e.g., USD, EUR, JPY) for the transaction. This must match the order's currency and must be a currency supported by the platform and the selected payment gateway. The currency determines how the payment gateway processes the transaction and affects settlement procedures.

provider.description:
Payment service provider that will process this transaction.

Examples: Stripe, PayPal, Square, Braintree. Identifies which payment processor's API will be used to process this transaction. The platform routes the payment request to the specified provider's API endpoint.

The provider selection is typically determined by the payment method type and platform configuration. Different providers may support different payment methods, currencies, and geographic regions. Required for routing the transaction to the correct payment gateway.

oneOf.description: Initial transaction status indicating processing in progress.
Transaction status indicating funds are successfully held.
Transaction status indicating payment completed successfully.
Transaction status indicating the payment provider rejected the transaction.
Transaction status indicating an authorization was cancelled.
Transaction status indicating captured funds were returned.

status.description:
Initial status of this payment transaction.

Valid values: pending, authorized, captured, failed, voided, refunded. Pending indicates processing in progress, authorized means funds are held, captured means payment completed. Failed indicates the payment provider rejected the transaction.

For new transaction creation, the typical initial status is 'pending' while the payment gateway processes the request. The status will be updated based on the provider's response to authorization or capture attempts.

provider_transaction_id.description:
Unique transaction identifier assigned by the payment provider.

Optional field that can be populated if the transaction ID is known at creation time or provided by the payment gateway during initial request. Typically null for new transaction creation and populated by the backend after receiving the provider's response.

Used for reconciliation with provider transaction records and dispute resolution. Required for successful transactions to enable refunds and chargebacks. When provided during creation, it helps link client-side payment initiation with server-side transaction recording.

Corresponds to the provider_transaction_id column in the shopping_mall_payment_transactions Prisma schema.

provider_response.description:
Raw JSON response from the payment provider for this transaction.

Optional field that can store the complete provider response if available during transaction creation. Typically null for new transactions and populated by the backend after payment gateway communication.

Stored for debugging, reconciliation, and regulatory compliance purposes. Contains provider-specific transaction details including authorization codes, risk scores, and additional metadata. Useful for investigating payment failures and resolving customer disputes.

Corresponds to the provider_response column in the shopping_mall_payment_transactions Prisma schema.

failure_reason.description:
Human-readable reason for transaction failure if status is failed.

Optional field typically null for new transaction creation and populated if the initial payment attempt fails. Examples include: insufficient_funds, card_declined, invalid_card, fraud_detected, network_error.

Helps customer support and buyers understand why payment didn't process. May be displayed to buyers or used for automated retry logic. The backend populates this based on the payment provider's error response.

Corresponds to the failure_reason column in the shopping_mall_payment_transactions Prisma schema.

failure_code.description:
Provider-specific error code for failed transactions.

Optional machine-readable code enabling detailed error analysis and conditional retry logic. Typically null for new transaction creation and populated if the payment provider returns an error code.

Used by payment processing system to determine if transaction should be retried automatically. Different providers use different error code formats and meanings. The backend maps provider error codes to this field for consistent error handling.

Corresponds to the failure_code column in the shopping_mall_payment_transactions Prisma schema.

ip_address.description:
IP address from which the payment is being initiated.

Captured for fraud detection, security auditing, and geographic analysis. Used to identify suspicious payment patterns and potential account compromise. Helps payment providers assess transaction risk and apply appropriate fraud prevention measures.

This field is optional but highly recommended for security. If not provided by the client, the server may capture it from the request headers. Including accurate IP address information improves fraud detection accuracy and may reduce payment decline rates.

user_agent.description:
Browser user agent string for the payment request.

Captured for fraud analysis and device fingerprinting. Helps identify automated attacks and unusual device patterns. Payment providers use this information as part of their risk assessment algorithms.

This field is optional but recommended for fraud prevention. The user agent string provides information about the buyer's browser and operating system, which can help detect suspicious activity patterns such as automated bot attacks or device spoofing attempts.

IShoppingMallPaymentTransaction.ICreate.description:
Data required to create a new payment transaction.

This DTO captures the essential information needed to initiate a payment transaction for an order during the checkout process. The buyer selects a saved payment method or enters payment details directly, and confirms the payment amount, which the system validates against the order total before creating the transaction record and submitting to the payment gateway.

The order context is provided through the URL path parameter (orderId) rather than in the request body, ensuring that payment transactions are always created within the context of a specific order. The authenticated buyer identity is derived from the JWT token, ensuring that buyers can only create payment transactions for their own orders.

Security validation includes verifying that the payment method belongs to the authenticated buyer (when provided), the amount matches the order total, and the currency is consistent throughout the order and payment flow. These validations prevent payment manipulation and ensure transaction integrity.

order.description:

IShoppingMallRefundTransaction.description:
Refund payment processing records for approved refund requests.

Records actual refund payment processing that occurs after refund requests are approved by admins or sellers.
This entity is distinct from refund requests which track buyer refund requests and approval workflow.

Each refund transaction represents a financial operation returning funds to the buyer through the payment provider.
Refund transactions reference both the original payment transaction being refunded and the refund request that authorized the refund.

Refunds can be full (entire order amount) or partial (percentage or specific amount based on refund reason).
The system tracks refund status through the payment provider lifecycle from initiation through completion or failure.

Refund transactions are immutable audit records that cannot be modified after creation.
All refund processing details including provider responses and timestamps are permanently logged for financial reconciliation and compliance.

End date of the period covered by this payout.

Orders completed on or before this date are eligible for inclusion.

gross_amount.description:
Total gross sales amount before commission deduction.

Sum of all order totals in the payout period before any fees or adjustments.

IShoppingMallSellerPayout.description:
Seller payout records for earnings settlement.

Tracks platform payouts to sellers for their completed sales after commission deduction.
Payouts aggregate earnings from multiple orders and are processed according to seller-configured payout schedules (weekly, bi-weekly, monthly).

Each payout record represents a single bank transfer or payment to the seller's verified account.
Payouts are held for 7 days after order delivery confirmation to protect against fraudulent transactions and allow time for buyer disputes.

The system calculates net payout amounts by summing order totals minus platform commissions for the payout period.
Payout status tracks the transfer lifecycle from pending through processing to completed or failed.

Sellers can view detailed payout history including which orders contributed to each payout and the commission breakdown.
All payout transactions are immutable audit records maintaining complete financial history for tax reporting and reconciliation.

id.description:
Primary Key. Unique identifier for the seller payout record.

This UUID serves as the immutable primary key for tracking individual payout transactions throughout their lifecycle from creation to completion or failure.

shopping_mall_seller_id.description:
Seller receiving this payout. Foreign key referencing shopping_mall_sellers.id.

Identifies which seller account this payout belongs to, establishing the ownership relationship between payouts and seller accounts. This field is essential for filtering seller-specific payout history and for administrators to identify payout ownership during financial reconciliation.

payout_period_start.description:
Start date of the period covered by this payout. Inclusive boundary for orders included in settlement.

Defines the beginning of the settlement period for which this payout aggregates seller earnings. All orders with completion dates on or after this timestamp are eligible for inclusion in the payout calculation.

payout_period_end.description:
End date of the period covered by this payout. Inclusive boundary for orders included in settlement.

Defines the end of the settlement period for which this payout aggregates seller earnings. All orders with completion dates on or before this timestamp are eligible for inclusion in the payout calculation. Together with payout_period_start, this establishes the complete settlement window.

gross_amount.description:
Total gross sales amount before commission deduction. Sum of all order totals in the payout period.

Represents the total revenue from all orders included in this settlement period before any platform fees, commissions, or adjustments are applied. This is the starting point for calculating the net payout amount and provides sellers with transparency into their total earnings.

commission_amount.description:
Total platform commission deducted from gross amount. Sum of all commission charges for included orders.

Represents the total platform fees charged on the orders in this settlement period. This amount is deducted from the gross_amount as part of calculating the net payout. The commission structure may vary based on seller tier, product category, or other business rules.

refund_amount.description:
Total refund amount deducted from payout. Refunds processed during the period reduce seller payout.

Represents refunds issued to customers during the settlement period that are deducted from the seller's earnings. These refunds reduce the net payout amount as the seller must return funds for cancelled or returned orders.

adjustment_amount.description:
Manual adjustments to payout amount. Can be positive (credits) or negative (charges). Examples: dispute resolutions, fee corrections.

Represents manual adjustments applied by platform administrators to correct errors, resolve disputes, or apply special credits or charges. Positive values increase the payout while negative values decrease it. This field ensures the payout system can handle exceptional cases and corrections.

net_payout_amount.description:
Final payout amount transferred to seller after all deductions. Calculated as gross_amount minus commission_amount minus refund_amount plus adjustment_amount.

Represents the actual funds transferred to the seller's bank account after platform commissions, refunds, and manual adjustments have been applied. This is the definitive settlement amount the seller receives.

currency.description:
Currency code for the payout amount. Three-letter ISO 4217 code.

Specifies the currency in which all monetary amounts in this payout are denominated, ensuring proper financial reporting and international transaction handling.

oneOf.description: Payout processing status tracking transfer lifecycle. Indicates payout is awaiting processing.
Payout processing status tracking transfer lifecycle. Indicates bank transfer is currently being processed.
Payout processing status tracking transfer lifecycle. Indicates funds have been successfully transferred to seller.
Payout processing status tracking transfer lifecycle. Indicates transfer failed and requires attention.

status.description:
Payout processing status tracking transfer lifecycle.

Tracks the current state of the payout from initial creation through bank transfer processing to final completion or failure. This status enables sellers to monitor payment progress and administrators to identify payouts requiring intervention.

bank_account_last_four.description:
Last four digits of seller's bank account receiving the payout. Used for seller verification and record-keeping.

Provides partial bank account information for sellers to verify which account received the payout without exposing the full account number. This field aids in payment reconciliation and helps sellers confirm payouts were sent to the correct account.

bank_name.description:
Name of the bank receiving the payout transfer. Captured for seller reference and audit purposes.

Provides the financial institution name where the payout funds are being transferred. This information helps sellers verify the transfer destination and assists with payment reconciliation when reviewing bank statements. The bank name is captured during payout processing and stored for audit trail purposes.

transfer_reference.description:
Bank transfer reference number or transaction ID. Used to track the transfer in banking systems.

Provides the unique identifier assigned by the banking system for this transfer transaction. Sellers can use this reference to trace the payment in their bank statements and resolve any discrepancies with their financial institution.

failure_reason.description:
Reason for payout failure if status is failed. Examples: invalid_account, insufficient_funds, bank_rejected. Null for successful payouts.

Provides diagnostic information explaining why a payout transfer failed, enabling sellers and administrators to understand the specific issue and take corrective action. Common failure reasons include invalid bank account details, insufficient platform funds, bank system rejections, or compliance holds. This field remains null for payouts that are pending, processing, or successfully completed.

notes.description:
Admin notes or explanations for adjustments and special circumstances. Used for documenting manual interventions.

Provides free-form text field for platform administrators to record explanations for manual payout adjustments, document special circumstances affecting the payout, or add context for unusual transactions. These notes create an audit trail for administrative actions and help future reviewers understand the reasoning behind payout modifications or special handling.

initiated_at.description:
Timestamp when the payout transfer was initiated with the banking system.

Records when the platform submitted the payout to the banking system for processing. This timestamp helps track processing timelines and identify delays between payout creation and bank transfer initiation.

completed_at.description:
Timestamp when the payout was successfully completed and funds transferred to seller. Null if still processing or failed.

Records the exact moment when the bank transfer was confirmed successful and funds became available in the seller's account. This timestamp is critical for financial reconciliation and for calculating actual payout delivery times.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this payout record was created. Immutable audit timestamp.

Records when the payout was initially created in the system, providing an audit trail for payout generation and enabling analysis of payout processing times.

IShoppingMallSellerPayout.ISummary.description:
Lightweight seller payout summary for list views and references.

Provides essential payout information including financial breakdown showing gross earnings, platform commissions, refunds, and adjustments that determine the net payout amount. Used in seller payout history lists and financial dashboard summaries.

Includes key identifiers, settlement period dates, complete financial breakdown (gross amount, commission, refunds, adjustments, net amount), processing status, payment tracking details (bank account reference, bank name, transfer ID, initiation timestamp), failure diagnostics, administrative notes, and completion timestamp. This comprehensive summary enables sellers to understand their earnings calculations and verify payment processing without requiring the full entity details.

IShoppingMallSellerPayout.IRequest.description:
Search and pagination parameters for filtering seller payout records.

Provides comprehensive filtering capabilities for locating seller payouts based on multiple criteria including payout status, settlement date ranges, processing timestamps, amount thresholds, and seller identification. This request schema supports both seller-facing earnings tracking and administrator financial reconciliation workflows.

The filtering system enables sellers to monitor their earnings settlements by date range, status, and amount while allowing administrators to search across all sellers for financial reporting and dispute resolution. Multiple date range filters support searching by settlement period (payout_date_from/to), transfer initiation (initiated_date_from/to), and completion (completed_date_from/to) to accommodate different temporal analysis needs. Pagination parameters ensure efficient handling of large payout datasets spanning multiple settlement cycles.

Sorting options allow users to organize payouts by settlement date, payout amount, processing status, or completion time to suit different analytical and monitoring needs.

page.description:
Page number for pagination, starting from 1.

Determines which page of payout results to return based on the configured page size. Essential for navigating through large datasets of historical payout records spanning multiple settlement periods.

limit.description:
Number of payout records to return per page.

Controls the page size for payout listings with a maximum of 100 records per page to balance performance and usability. Typical values range from 10-50 for dashboard displays and financial reports.

seller_id.description:
Filter payouts by specific seller account identifier.

Restricts results to payouts for a particular seller account. This filter is automatically applied when sellers access their own payout history, while administrators can use it to view payouts for any seller during support or audit activities.

Allows users to find payouts in specific workflow states such as pending settlements awaiting processing, completed transfers, or failed transactions requiring attention. This filter is essential for monitoring payment processing health and identifying issues.

min_amount.description:
Minimum net payout amount threshold for filtering.

Finds payouts with net amounts greater than or equal to this value. Useful for identifying large settlements, filtering out small payouts, or analyzing earnings distribution across different revenue tiers.

max_amount.description:
Maximum net payout amount threshold for filtering.

Finds payouts with net amounts less than or equal to this value. Can be combined with min_amount to define specific payout amount ranges for financial analysis and reporting.

payout_date_from.description:
Start date for payout period range filtering.

Filters payouts with settlement periods starting on or after this date. Essential for generating period-specific financial reports, tracking monthly settlements, or analyzing payout trends over time.

payout_date_to.description:
End date for payout period range filtering.

Filters payouts with settlement periods ending on or before this date. Combined with payout_date_from to define specific settlement periods for accounting reconciliation and earnings tracking.

initiated_date_from.description:
Start date for filtering by payout initiation timestamp.

Finds payouts that were initiated with the banking system on or after this date. Useful for tracking when payouts entered the bank transfer process and analyzing processing pipeline performance.

initiated_date_to.description:
End date for filtering by payout initiation timestamp.

Finds payouts that were initiated with the banking system on or before this date. Combined with initiated_date_from to analyze payouts initiated within specific time windows.

completed_date_from.description:
Start date for filtering by payout completion timestamp.

Finds payouts that were successfully completed on or after this date. Essential for financial reconciliation showing when funds actually arrived in seller accounts.

completed_date_to.description:
End date for filtering by payout completion timestamp.

Finds payouts that were successfully completed on or before this date. Combined with completed_date_from to analyze payouts completed within specific time windows and measure processing durations.

search.description:
Free-text search across payout-related fields.

Searches through seller names, transfer references, notes, and other text fields to find payouts matching the search query. Provides flexible discovery when specific filter criteria are unknown or when searching by partial information.

oneOf.description: Sort by settlement period start date for chronological ordering.
Sort by settlement period end date for chronological ordering.
Sort by net payout amount for financial analysis.
Sort by processing status for workflow management.
Sort by completion timestamp for tracking transfer timing.
Sort by creation timestamp for audit trail ordering.

sort_by.description:
Field to use for sorting payout results.

Determines which payout attribute is used as the primary sort key. Common choices include payout_period_start for chronological ordering, net_payout_amount for financial analysis, or status for workflow management.

oneOf.description: Sort in ascending order (oldest/smallest first).
Sort in descending order (newest/largest first).

sort_order.description:
Sort direction for ordered results.

Specifies whether payouts should be sorted in ascending (oldest/smallest first) or descending (newest/largest first) order based on the selected sort_by field.

shopping_mall_seller_id.description:
Reference to the seller account receiving this payout.

Identifies which seller will receive the earnings settlement. This must correspond to a valid seller account in the shopping_mall_sellers table. The system validates that the seller exists, is active, and has sufficient earnings balance before processing the payout.

This is a foreign key relationship to shopping_mall_sellers.id. Required field for initiating any payout transaction.

payout_period_start.description:
Start date of the period covered by this payout.

Inclusive boundary for orders included in settlement. Orders completed on or after this date are eligible for inclusion in this payout calculation. Defines the beginning of the earnings calculation window.

Must be a valid ISO 8601 date-time. Typically aligns with seller's configured payout schedule (weekly, bi-weekly, or monthly periods).

payout_period_end.description:
End date of the period covered by this payout.

Inclusive boundary for orders included in settlement. Orders completed on or before this date are eligible for inclusion in this payout calculation. Defines the end of the earnings calculation window.

Must be a valid ISO 8601 date-time. Must be after payout_period_start. System enforces 7-day holding period after delivery confirmation before including orders in payouts.

gross_amount.description:
Total gross sales amount before commission deduction.

Sum of all order totals in the payout period before any fees or adjustments. Represents total revenue generated by seller during the period. Used as the basis for calculating platform commission and net payout amounts.

Must be a non-negative number. Calculated by summing all completed order totals within the payout period that meet the holding period requirements.

commission_amount.description:
Total platform commission deducted from gross amount.

Sum of all commission charges for included orders based on platform fee structure. Commission rates may vary by product category, seller tier, or promotional agreements. This amount is deducted from gross_amount to calculate net payout.

Must be a non-negative number. Cannot exceed gross_amount. Calculated according to platform commission policies and seller-specific rate agreements.

refund_amount.description:
Total refund amount deducted from payout.

Refunds processed during the period reduce seller payout to account for returned funds. Includes both full and partial refunds for orders in this payout period. Ensures sellers are not paid for cancelled or refunded transactions.

Must be a non-negative number. Represents the total value of buyer refunds that must be recovered from seller earnings during this payout cycle.

adjustment_amount.description:
Manual adjustments to payout amount.

Can be positive (credits) or negative (charges) based on administrative actions. Examples include dispute resolutions, fee corrections, promotional credits, penalty charges, or other exceptional circumstances requiring manual intervention.

Can be positive, negative, or zero. Should be documented in the notes field for transparency and audit purposes. Requires administrative authorization for non-zero values.

net_payout_amount.description:
Final payout amount transferred to seller.

Calculated as gross_amount minus commission_amount minus refund_amount plus adjustment_amount. Represents actual funds transferred to seller's bank account or payment method. This is the amount seller receives after all deductions and adjustments.

Must be non-negative (system may block payouts with negative net amounts). Should match the bank transfer amount exactly for reconciliation purposes.

currency.description:
Currency code for all amounts in this payout.

Three-letter ISO 4217 code used consistently across all monetary fields (gross_amount, commission_amount, refund_amount, adjustment_amount, net_payout_amount). Determines currency of bank transfer to seller account.

Examples: USD, EUR, GBP, JPY. Must match the seller's configured payout currency and supported currencies in the payment gateway.

status.description:
Initial payout processing status.

Tracks bank transfer lifecycle from creation through completion. For new payout creation, typically set to 'pending' indicating payout has been calculated but not yet initiated with the banking system.

Valid values: pending, processing, completed, failed. Status transitions are managed by the payment processing workflow and updated through subsequent API calls.

bank_account_last_four.description:
Last four digits of seller's bank account receiving the payout.

Used for seller verification and record-keeping without exposing full account number. Helps sellers confirm payout destination for security. Captured at payout creation for audit trail purposes.

Optional field. If provided, should contain exactly 4 numeric characters. Null if bank account information not available or payout method doesn't use bank transfer.

bank_name.description:
Name of the bank receiving the payout transfer.

Captured for seller reference and audit purposes. Helps sellers identify which account will receive funds. Used in payout confirmation notifications and financial reporting.

Optional field. Null if bank information not available or not applicable to payout method. Should match seller's verified banking information on file.

transfer_reference.description:
Bank transfer reference number or transaction ID.

Used to track the transfer in banking systems for reconciliation. Provides external reference for investigating payout status or issues. May be generated by payment gateway or banking system.

Optional field at creation. Typically null for new payout requests and populated later when payment processor initiates the transfer and returns a transaction reference ID.

failure_reason.description:
Reason for payout failure if status is failed.

Examples: invalid_account, insufficient_funds, bank_rejected, account_closed, verification_failed. Provides actionable information for resolving failed transfers. Used to communicate issues to sellers and support teams.

Optional field. Should be null for new payout creation (as status is typically pending). Populated only when payout processing encounters errors and status transitions to failed.

initiated_at.description:
Timestamp when the payout transfer was initiated with the banking system.

Marks when transfer request was submitted to bank or payment processor. Used to track transfer processing time and identify delays. Important for SLA monitoring and operational analytics.

Optional field at creation. Typically null for new payout records in pending status. Populated when payout status transitions to processing and bank transfer is actually initiated.

completed_at.description:
Timestamp when the payout was successfully completed and funds transferred to seller.

Marks when funds became available in seller's bank account. Used for seller notifications, financial reconciliation, and payout history tracking. Critical for calculating actual payout delivery times.

Optional field at creation. Must be null for new payout records. Populated only when payout status transitions to completed and payment processor confirms successful fund transfer.

notes.description:
Administrative notes or explanations for the payout creation.

Free-text field for recording context, special instructions, or explanatory information about why this payout is being created. Useful for documenting manual payouts, special circumstances, exceptional calculations, or administrative decisions.

Optional field. Helps maintain clear audit trails and operational transparency. Particularly important when adjustment_amount is non-zero or when creating payouts outside normal automated schedules.

IShoppingMallSellerPayout.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new seller payout transaction.

Contains the complete financial information needed to initiate a payment settlement to a seller account. This DTO specifies which seller should receive payment, the earnings period covered, detailed amount breakdowns, and the final payout calculation.

The payout creation request includes all financial components required for transparent earnings settlement: gross sales, platform commissions, refunds, manual adjustments, and net payout amount. The platform validates all calculations, verifies seller account status, and ensures data integrity before creating the payout record.

Security note: This operation requires administrative authorization as it involves financial fund transfers. The system validates that gross_amount minus commission_amount minus refund_amount plus adjustment_amount equals net_payout_amount. It also verifies seller account existence, earnings balance sufficiency, and amount consistency.

Used in administrative payout processing workflows and automated settlement systems for transferring accumulated seller earnings to their registered payment accounts. Initial status is typically set to pending, with subsequent status updates handled through the update operation as payment processing progresses.

payout_period_start.description:
Updated start date of the period covered by this payout.

Allows correction of the payout period boundary if initial calculation window was incorrect. Modifying this field may require recalculation of gross_amount and other derived amounts to ensure accuracy.

Typically only modifiable for pending payouts that haven't been processed. Changes to completed payout periods may require special authorization and audit documentation.

payout_period_end.description:
Updated end date of the period covered by this payout.

Allows correction of the payout period boundary if initial calculation window was incorrect. Modifying this field may require recalculation of gross_amount and other derived amounts to ensure accuracy.

Typically only modifiable for pending payouts that haven't been processed. Must maintain date logic where payout_period_end is after payout_period_start.

gross_amount.description:
Updated total gross sales amount before commission deduction.

Allows correction of the gross earnings calculation if initial amount was incorrect due to data inconsistencies or late-arriving order updates. Modifications typically trigger recalculation of net_payout_amount.

Amount modifications are typically restricted to pending or failed payouts. Changes to completed payouts may require elevated authorization and detailed audit trail documentation.

commission_amount.description:
Updated total platform commission deducted from gross amount.

Allows correction of commission calculations if rate changes were applied incorrectly or if seller tier adjustments need to be reflected. Modifications affect net_payout_amount calculation.

Must be non-negative and should not exceed gross_amount. Changes typically require administrative authorization and documentation in notes field.

refund_amount.description:
Updated total refund amount deducted from payout.

Allows adjustment if additional refunds were processed after initial payout calculation or if refund amounts were calculated incorrectly. Increases reduce net_payout_amount to recover refunded funds from seller.

Must be non-negative. Changes should be documented in notes field explaining the refund adjustments and timing.

adjustment_amount.description:
Updated manual adjustments to payout amount.

Allows modification of credits or charges applied for dispute resolutions, fee corrections, promotional programs, or penalty assessments. Can be positive (credits to seller) or negative (charges against seller).

All adjustment changes should be documented in notes field with clear business justification. Significant adjustments may require elevated administrative authorization.

net_payout_amount.description:
Updated final payout amount transferred to seller.

Allows direct correction of the final payout value if calculation errors occurred. Should be recalculated when any component amounts (gross, commission, refund, adjustment) are modified to maintain calculation integrity.

Must be non-negative. System may validate that net_payout_amount equals gross_amount minus commission_amount minus refund_amount plus adjustment_amount.

currency.description:
Updated currency code for all amounts in this payout.

Allows correction if payout was created with incorrect currency. Changing currency typically requires recalculation of all amount fields using current exchange rates.

Must be valid three-letter ISO 4217 code. Currency changes are typically restricted to pending payouts and may require special authorization.

status.description:
Updated processing status of the payout transaction.

Allows administrators to modify the payout status as it progresses through the payment lifecycle. Common status transitions include moving from pending to processing, processing to completed, or marking failed payouts.

Valid values: pending, processing, completed, failed. Status updates must follow valid business rules for state transitions. For example, completed payouts typically cannot be reverted to pending status. The system validates status transition logic before applying updates.

bank_account_last_four.description:
Updated last four digits of seller's bank account.

Allows correction if bank account information was captured incorrectly or if seller changed their payout destination account. Used for verification and audit trail purposes.

Typically only modifiable for pending payouts. Should contain exactly 4 numeric characters when provided. Changes should be documented in notes field.

bank_name.description:
Updated name of the bank receiving the payout transfer.

Allows correction if bank information was captured incorrectly or if seller changed their banking institution. Used for seller reference and audit trail purposes.

Typically only modifiable for pending payouts. Changes should align with updated bank_account_last_four and be documented in notes field.

transfer_reference.description:
Updated bank transfer reference number or transaction ID.

Typically populated by administrators when receiving transaction confirmation from payment processors. This field is commonly updated when moving payouts from pending/processing to completed status.

May also be updated to correct erroneous transaction IDs or to link payouts with external payment system records. Critical for payment reconciliation and issue investigation.

failure_reason.description:
Updated reason for payout failure.

Typically populated when setting status to failed, documenting why the bank transfer could not complete. Examples: invalid_account, insufficient_funds, bank_rejected, account_closed, verification_failed.

Provides actionable information for resolving failed transfers. Should be set to null when clearing failed status or when payout is successfully reprocessed.

initiated_at.description:
Updated timestamp when the payout transfer was initiated.

Set when payout status transitions to processing and transfer request is submitted to banking system. May be updated to correct timestamp errors or when backdating initiated payouts.

Used to track transfer processing time and identify delays. Important for SLA monitoring and operational analytics.

completed_at.description:
Updated processing completion timestamp.

Set when marking a payout as completed, recording the exact moment the payment processor successfully transferred funds. Administrators may also update this field when backdating completed payouts or correcting processing timestamps.

Typically updated in conjunction with status changes to completed. Critical for payout history tracking and financial reconciliation. May be set to null when reverting completed status.

notes.description:
Updated or additional administrative notes.

Allows administrators to add context about status changes, record resolution details for problematic payouts, or document reasons for amount adjustments. Notes can be appended or completely replaced based on operational needs.

Supports comprehensive audit trails and operational transparency. Particularly important when documenting manual interventions, special circumstances, or deviations from standard processing workflows.

IShoppingMallSellerPayout.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating an existing seller payout record.

Contains modifiable fields that administrators can update to reflect payout processing progress, correct payout information, or resolve payment issues. All fields are optional, allowing partial updates to specific payout attributes without affecting other data.

Common update scenarios include status progression as payments process through payment gateways, adding transfer references received from payment processors, recording processing completion timestamps, adjusting amounts due to calculation corrections or late-arriving data, and documenting administrative actions through notes.

Security considerations: Payout updates require administrative authorization due to financial implications. The system enforces business rules for valid status transitions, restricts amount modifications based on payout state, and maintains complete audit trails of all changes. Updates to completed payouts may require elevated permissions or be prohibited based on platform policies.

Immutable fields excluded from updates include the payout ID (system identifier), shopping_mall_seller_id (ownership assignment), and created_at timestamp (historical record). These fields preserve payout integrity and financial audit trail accuracy.

Used in payout management workflows for tracking payment processing progress, resolving payment issues, correcting data errors, and maintaining accurate financial settlement records.

IShoppingMallPlatformCommission.description:
Platform commission record representing the marketplace fee charged on seller transactions.

This entity captures the platform's revenue from facilitating transactions between buyers and sellers. Each commission record is an immutable audit entry tracking the commission amount, rate applied, calculation basis, and payment processing details for a specific order transaction.

Platform commissions are calculated as a percentage of the order subtotal and recorded when payment transactions are completed. The commission type field indicates which rate structure was applied (standard, category-specific, seller-tier-based, or promotional).

This table serves as the authoritative source for platform revenue reporting, financial reconciliation, seller settlement calculations, and commission refund tracking when orders are cancelled or refunded.

id.description:
Primary key identifier for the platform commission record.

Unique UUID auto-generated for each commission entry in the shopping_mall_platform_commissions table. Ensures globally unique identification of commission transactions across the entire marketplace platform.

Used for direct commission record retrieval, financial reporting queries, and audit trail tracking.

shopping_mall_payment_transaction_id.description:
Foreign key reference to the payment transaction that generated this commission.

Links to shopping_mall_payment_transactions.id to establish the relationship between payment processing and commission calculation. Each commission record is uniquely associated with exactly one payment transaction.

This relationship enables tracking of commission revenue back to the original payment event and supports financial reconciliation between payment processing and platform earnings.

shopping_mall_order_id.description:
Foreign key reference to the parent order associated with this commission.

Links to shopping_mall_orders.id to connect commission records with the order transactions that generated them. Enables commission tracking and revenue attribution at the order level.

Used for order-based financial reporting, commission history queries, and dispute resolution requiring order context.

shopping_mall_seller_id.description:
Foreign key reference to the seller from whose transaction this commission was earned.

Links to shopping_mall_sellers.id to identify which merchant's sale generated this platform revenue. Essential for seller-specific commission tracking and payout calculations.

Supports seller performance analytics, commission rate analysis by seller tier, and seller settlement reconciliation.

order_subtotal.description:
Order subtotal amount before shipping and taxes used as the commission calculation base.

Represents the total value of items in the order excluding shipping costs and tax amounts. This is the base amount to which the commission rate is applied to calculate the commission.

Stored separately from commission_amount to enable commission recalculation verification and support financial audits requiring detailed commission calculation breakdowns.

commission_rate.description:
Commission rate percentage applied to this transaction, stored as a decimal fraction.

Decimal value between 0.0 and 1.0 representing the percentage of order_subtotal charged as platform commission. For example, 0.15 represents a 15% commission rate.

This rate may vary based on product category, seller tier, promotional periods, or negotiated agreements. Recording the actual rate applied ensures accurate historical commission tracking even when platform rate structures change over time.

commission_amount.description:
Calculated commission amount earned by the platform from this transaction.

Monetary value computed by multiplying order_subtotal by commission_rate. Represents the platform's revenue from facilitating this transaction, which is deducted from the seller's payout.

This amount is the actual platform earnings and is used for revenue reporting, financial statements, and seller settlement calculations.

currency.description:
Currency code for all monetary amounts in this commission record.

Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP) that applies to order_subtotal, commission_amount, and refunded_amount fields. Must match the currency used in the associated order.

Ensures consistent currency interpretation across all financial values in the commission record and supports multi-currency marketplace operations.

commission_type.description:
Type of commission calculation structure applied to this transaction.

Indicates which commission rate methodology was used: 'standard' (default platform rate), 'category_specific' (product category-based rate), 'seller_tier' (seller performance tier rate), or 'promotional' (special promotional rate).

Documenting the commission type enables analysis of revenue by rate structure, supports commission policy audits, and maintains transparency in how platform fees are calculated across different scenarios.

is_refunded.description:
Flag indicating whether this commission has been reversed due to order refund.

Set to true when the associated order is refunded and the commission revenue is reversed. Set to false for all active commission records where the platform retains the fee.

Used for net revenue calculations, financial reporting that excludes refunded commissions, and reconciliation of platform earnings with actual collected revenue.

refunded_amount.description:
Commission amount that has been refunded to the seller due to order cancellation or refund.

Contains the monetary value of commission reversed when partial or full order refunds occur. Zero when no refund has been processed (is_refunded is false). May equal commission_amount for full refunds or be less for partial refunds.

Essential for calculating net commission revenue, tracking refund-related commission adjustments, and maintaining accurate platform earnings after refund processing.

created_at.description:
Immutable timestamp recording when this commission record was created in the system.

ISO 8601 formatted date-time indicating when this commission entry was generated, typically corresponding to payment transaction completion or order processing.

Used for financial reporting period attribution, chronological commission tracking, audit trail maintenance, and temporal analysis of platform revenue patterns.

IShoppingMallPlatformCommission.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary representation of platform commission records for list views and financial reports.

Provides essential commission information optimized for displaying platform revenue entries in administrative dashboards, commission tracking interfaces, and seller payout reconciliation views where complete transaction details are not required.

This DTO variant includes all key financial metrics and identifiers while excluding deeply nested relationship data, ensuring efficient data transfer for high-volume commission listing scenarios.

id.description:
Primary key identifier for the platform commission record.

Unique UUID serving as the primary key in the shopping_mall_platform_commissions table for tracking individual commission transactions in the platform revenue accounting system.

Used for commission record retrieval, detail view navigation, and financial record cross-referencing.

shopping_mall_payment_transaction_id.description:
Foreign key reference to the payment transaction that generated this commission.

Links to shopping_mall_payment_transactions.id, identifying the specific payment event from which this platform revenue was derived.

Enables payment-to-commission tracing and supports financial reconciliation between payment processing and commission accounting.

shopping_mall_order_id.description:
Foreign key reference to the parent order that generated this commission.

Links to shopping_mall_orders.id, connecting this commission record to the order transaction that produced the platform revenue.

Used for order-based commission queries and revenue attribution analysis.

shopping_mall_seller_id.description:
Foreign key reference to the seller whose transaction generated this commission.

Links to shopping_mall_sellers.id, identifying which merchant's sale contributed to this platform revenue entry.

Supports seller-specific commission reporting and payout reconciliation workflows.

order_subtotal.description:
Order subtotal amount used as the base for commission calculation.

Represents the pre-shipping, pre-tax order value to which the commission rate was applied. Displayed in summary views to provide context for commission amount calculations.

Useful for understanding commission calculation basis without requiring full order details.

commission_rate.description:
Commission rate applied to this transaction as a decimal fraction.

Decimal value between 0.0 and 1.0 representing the percentage of order value retained by the platform (e.g., 0.15 for 15% commission).

Displayed in summary views to show the rate structure applied to each transaction for transparency and rate analysis.

commission_amount.description:
Actual commission amount earned by the platform from this transaction.

Calculated monetary value representing the platform's revenue, expressed in the currency specified by the currency field. Must be non-negative.

Core financial metric displayed in all commission summaries and revenue reports.

currency.description:
ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for monetary amounts.

Indicates the currency for order_subtotal, commission_amount, and refunded_amount values (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP).

Essential for proper financial amount interpretation in multi-currency marketplace environments.

commission_type.description:
Commission calculation structure type applied.

Indicates which rate methodology was used: standard, category_specific, seller_tier, or promotional.

Provides context for commission amount calculations and supports revenue analysis by commission type.

is_refunded.description:
Refund status flag for this commission record.

Indicates whether this commission has been reversed due to order refund (true) or remains as active platform revenue (false).

Critical for distinguishing between gross and net commission revenue in financial reports.

refunded_amount.description:
Commission amount refunded due to order cancellation or refund.

Monetary value of commission reversed, expressed in the same currency as commission_amount. Zero when no refund has occurred.

Used for calculating net commission revenue and tracking refund-related adjustments.

created_at.description:
Commission record creation timestamp.

ISO 8601 formatted date-time recording when this commission entry was generated in the platform accounting system.

Used for chronological sorting, financial period attribution, and temporal revenue analysis.

page.description:
Page number for pagination, starting from 1.

Determines which page of results to return based on the limit parameter.

Defaults to 1 if not specified.

limit.description:
Number of commission records to return per page.

Controls the page size for pagination, with a maximum of 100 records per request to ensure reasonable response times.

Defaults to 20 if not specified.

order_id.description:
Filter commission records by specific order identifier.

When provided, returns only commission records associated with the specified order.

Useful for viewing all commission details related to a particular order transaction.

seller_id.description:
Filter commission records by specific seller identifier.

When provided, returns only commission records for transactions from the specified seller.

Essential for seller-specific commission reporting and revenue analysis.

commission_type.description:
Filter by commission calculation type.

Valid values: 'standard', 'category_specific', 'seller_tier', 'promotional'.

Allows analysis of revenue by commission structure and rate category.

is_refunded.description:
Filter by refund status.

When true, returns only refunded commission records. When false, returns only non-refunded records.

Critical for separating gross revenue from net revenue after refund adjustments.

currency.description:
Filter commission records by currency code.

When provided, returns only commission records denominated in the specified currency. Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code format (e.g., 'USD', 'EUR', 'GBP').

Essential for multi-currency marketplaces to separate revenue streams by currency and ensure accurate financial reporting without currency mixing. Enables currency-specific revenue analysis and facilitates proper accounting treatment for international transactions.

min_commission_amount.description:
Minimum commission amount filter for range-based searching.

Returns records where commission_amount is greater than or equal to this value.

Useful for identifying high-value commission transactions.

max_commission_amount.description:
Maximum commission amount filter for range-based searching.

Returns records where commission_amount is less than or equal to this value.

Enables filtering by commission value ranges for financial analysis.

min_refunded_amount.description:
Minimum refunded amount filter for commission refund analysis.

Returns records where refunded_amount is greater than or equal to this value. Filters for commissions that have been partially or fully reversed due to order refunds.

Used in conjunction with is_refunded filter to analyze the financial impact of refunds on platform revenue. Enables identification of significant refund events and assessment of refund patterns affecting commission income.

max_refunded_amount.description:
Maximum refunded amount filter for commission refund analysis.

Returns records where refunded_amount is less than or equal to this value. Completes the range filtering capability for refunded commission amounts.

Enables precise refund impact analysis by defining upper bounds on refund values. Useful for filtering out major refund events or focusing on specific refund amount ranges in revenue reconciliation processes.

min_order_subtotal.description:
Minimum order subtotal filter for transaction size analysis.

Returns records where order_subtotal is greater than or equal to this value. Filters commissions based on the underlying order value that served as the commission calculation basis.

Enables analysis of commission revenue by transaction size segments. Useful for identifying commission patterns from high-value versus low-value orders, supporting pricing strategy evaluation and seller tier analysis.

max_order_subtotal.description:
Maximum order subtotal filter for transaction size analysis.

Returns records where order_subtotal is less than or equal to this value. Completes the range filtering capability for order transaction values.

Enables targeted analysis of commission revenue from specific order value brackets. Supports segmentation of revenue streams by transaction size and evaluation of commission rate effectiveness across different order value ranges.

created_after.description:
Filter for commission records created on or after this timestamp.

Enables date range filtering for revenue reporting by time period.

ISO 8601 format required (e.g., '2024-01-01T00:00:00Z').

created_before.description:
Filter for commission records created on or before this timestamp.

Enables date range filtering for revenue reporting by time period.

ISO 8601 format required (e.g., '2024-12-31T23:59:59Z').

oneOf.description:
Field to sort results by.

Valid options: 'created_at' (chronological order), 'commission_amount' (revenue size), 'order_subtotal' (order value).

Defaults to 'created_at' if not specified.

Field to sort results by.

Valid options: 'created_at' (chronological order), 'commission_amount' (revenue size), 'order_subtotal' (order value).

Defaults to 'created_at' if not specified.

Field to sort results by.

Valid options: 'created_at' (chronological order), 'commission_amount' (revenue size), 'order_subtotal' (order value).

Defaults to 'created_at' if not specified.

sort_by.description:
Field to sort results by.

Valid options: 'created_at' (chronological order), 'commission_amount' (revenue size), 'order_subtotal' (order value).

Defaults to 'created_at' if not specified.

oneOf.description:
Sort direction for the results.

Valid options: 'asc' (ascending, oldest/smallest first), 'desc' (descending, newest/largest first).

Defaults to 'desc' for created_at sorting, showing most recent commissions first.

Sort direction for the results.

Valid options: 'asc' (ascending, oldest/smallest first), 'desc' (descending, newest/largest first).

Defaults to 'desc' for created_at sorting, showing most recent commissions first.

sort_order.description:
Sort direction for the results.

Valid options: 'asc' (ascending, oldest/smallest first), 'desc' (descending, newest/largest first).

Defaults to 'desc' for created_at sorting, showing most recent commissions first.

IShoppingMallPlatformCommission.IRequest.description:
Search and filter parameters for retrieving platform commission records.

Provides comprehensive filtering capabilities for commission record queries including date ranges, commission amounts, order references, seller attribution, and commission calculation types. Supports flexible pagination and sorting to enable detailed financial reporting and revenue analysis.

All filter parameters are optional, allowing queries ranging from broad unfiltered lists to highly specific targeted searches. Combining multiple filters enables sophisticated financial analysis such as seller-specific revenue trends, commission type performance, and refund impact assessment.

IShoppingMallPlatformCommissions.description:
Collection of platform commission records.

Represents an array of platform commission entries associated with orders in the marketplace. Each commission record captures the platform's fee for facilitating transactions between buyers and sellers.

In multi-seller marketplace systems, orders may contain items from multiple sellers, resulting in multiple commission records per order. This type provides the structure for returning collections of commission data for administrative financial tracking, revenue reporting, and audit purposes.

Used in response bodies for operations that retrieve commission records, enabling administrators to analyze platform revenue, verify seller transaction fees, and perform financial reconciliation.

data.description:
Array of platform commission records associated with the order.

Each element represents a single commission entry capturing the platform's fee for a specific transaction or seller portion of an order. In marketplace systems with multiple sellers per order, this array contains one commission record per seller's items.

The collection enables comprehensive financial tracking by providing complete commission breakdowns for order-level revenue analysis and seller payout calculations.

IShoppingMallRevenueStatistics.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for revenue statistics analytics query.

Defines the filtering, grouping, and time range parameters for retrieving aggregated revenue metrics and financial analytics. Supports flexible business intelligence queries across multiple dimensions including time periods, seller segments, product categories, and transaction types.

This request type enables administrators to customize revenue reports by specifying date ranges, aggregation granularity, and filtering criteria to analyze platform financial performance from various perspectives.

start_date.description:
Start date for the analytics period (inclusive).

ISO 8601 date format (YYYY-MM-DD) marking the beginning of the time range for revenue aggregation. All transactions with created_at timestamps on or after this date will be included in the analysis.

Required to define the temporal scope of the revenue report.

end_date.description:
