Complements from_created_at to define the upper bound of the time range. Only votes with created_at less than or equal to this value are included.

Enables analysis of historical voting patterns and identification of vote manipulation attempts during specific timeframes.

sort_by.description:
Field to sort results by.

Determines which field is used for ordering the vote list. Options include created_at (submission time) or is_helpful (vote type).

When null or omitted, defaults to created_at in descending order (newest first).

order.description:
Sort direction for results.

Specifies whether results should be sorted in ascending (asc) or descending (desc) order based on the sort_by field.

When null or omitted, defaults to descending order (desc) to show most recent votes first.

IShoppingMallReviewHelpfulnessVote.IRequ.description:

This request DTO provides comprehensive search capabilities for retrieving helpfulness votes with pagination, filtering, and sorting options. All parameters are optional, allowing flexible query construction based on specific analysis needs.

The pagination parameters (page, limit) control result set size and navigation. Filtering parameters (is_helpful, shopping_mall_buyer_id, timestamp ranges) enable targeted data retrieval. Sorting parameters (sort_by, order) control result ordering.

This DTO is used in the search operation to analyze vote patterns, identify voting trends, and retrieve specific subsets of votes for display or analytics purposes.

Contains only the buyer's binary assessment of whether the review was helpful. The authenticated buyer's identity is automatically extracted from the JWT token, and the target review is identified by the reviewId path parameter. System-managed fields like id, timestamps, and foreign keys are automatically populated by the backend.

This minimal DTO design ensures buyers can quickly submit their helpfulness assessment with a single required field. The operation enforces business rules including preventing duplicate votes and validating that the target review exists and is published.

IShoppingMallReviewReport.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering parameters for retrieving review reports with pagination.

Provides comprehensive query capabilities for finding and managing review reports submitted by users flagging reviews for policy violations. Supports pagination, sorting, and multiple filter criteria to enable efficient moderation workflows for administrators.

Pagination parameters (page, limit) control result set size and enable navigation through large numbers of reports. Sorting options (sort_by, sort_order) allow organizing reports by submission date, moderation status, or violation category. Filter criteria narrow results based on reason, status, reporter, submission date ranges, and admin review timestamps.

All parameters are optional, with sensible defaults applied when omitted. The operation returns a paginated response containing report summaries matching the specified criteria. This DTO design balances flexibility for complex queries with simplicity for common use cases like viewing recent pending reports.

id.description:

shopping_mall_review_id.description:

Foreign key reference to shopping_mall_reviews.id. Links this report to the specific product review that is being flagged for policy violations such as spam, offensive content, fake reviews, or irrelevant feedback.

This association enables moderators to quickly navigate from the report to the actual review content for investigation and decision-making.

reporter_buyer_id.description:
Buyer who submitted the report, if reporter is a buyer.

Foreign key reference to shopping_mall_buyers.id. When a buyer submits a report, this field contains their unique identifier while reporter_seller_id is null.

Either reporter_buyer_id or reporter_seller_id must be populated, but not both. This implements the reporter pattern where both buyers and sellers can report problematic reviews to maintain platform quality.

reporter_seller_id.description:

Foreign key reference to shopping_mall_sellers.id. When a seller submits a report, this field contains their unique identifier while reporter_buyer_id is null.

Either reporter_buyer_id or reporter_seller_id must be populated, but not both. Sellers can report reviews on any products in the marketplace, not just their own listings, to help maintain overall review quality and combat fraudulent reviews.

report_details.description:

Free-text field allowing the reporter to provide context and specifics about the policy violation. Maximum 1000 characters.

Provides additional information for admin investigation beyond the predefined reason category. Helps moderators understand the specific concern and make informed decisions about review visibility and user actions.

status.description:

Indicates the current state in the moderation workflow. Valid values: pending, reviewed_valid, reviewed_invalid, dismissed.

'pending' - Awaiting admin investigation. 'reviewed_valid' - Admin confirmed the violation and took action. 'reviewed_invalid' - Admin determined the report was unfounded. 'dismissed' - Report was closed without action (e.g., duplicate report, reporter withdrew complaint).

created_at.description:

reviewed_at.description:

Set when admin completes investigation and makes moderation decision. Null for reports still in pending status.

Used to calculate moderation response time, track admin productivity, and provide transparency to reporters about when their submission was processed. The difference between created_at and reviewed_at represents the time the report spent in the moderation queue.

IShoppingMallReviewReport.description:
User-submitted report flagging a review for policy violations.

Represents a complete report record from the shopping_mall_review_reports table. Both buyers and sellers can report reviews they believe violate platform policies including spam, offensive content, fake reviews, or irrelevant feedback.

Each report requires a reason category selection and optional detailed explanation to help admins investigate. Reports are routed to the admin moderation queue for manual review. Multiple reports on the same review escalate priority and may trigger automatic temporary hiding pending admin investigation.

The system tracks report patterns to identify users who abuse the reporting system and legitimate reviews that are frequently falsely reported. This dual accountability ensures both review quality and reporter integrity.

Relationships: Each report references exactly one review (shopping_mall_review_id) and is submitted by either a buyer (reporter_buyer_id) or seller (reporter_seller_id), but not both. The report may trigger moderation actions recorded in shopping_mall_review_moderation_logs.

Lifecycle: Reports are created with 'pending' status, transition through admin investigation (reviewed_valid, reviewed_invalid, dismissed), and serve as permanent audit trails of community-driven content moderation.

report_reason.description:
Reason category for the report.

Specify the predefined category that best describes the policy violation. Valid values: spam, offensive_language, fake_review, not_about_product, personal_information, other.

This classification helps moderators prioritize reports and route them to appropriate handling workflows. Choose the most specific category that matches the violation to ensure efficient processing.

report_details.description:
Optional detailed explanation of the policy violation.

Provide specific context about why this review violates platform policies. Maximum 1000 characters.

This free-text field allows you to elaborate beyond the predefined reason category. Include specific examples, quotes from the review, or circumstances that help moderators understand your concern and make informed decisions.

IShoppingMallReviewReport.ICreate.description:
Request body for submitting a new review report.

Captures the minimal information required from authenticated users (buyers or sellers) to report a policy-violating review. The report creation process validates that the review exists and the reporter is properly authenticated.

Security: The reporter identity (buyer_id or seller_id) is automatically extracted from the JWT authentication token and must never be included in the request body. The reviewId is provided as a path parameter, not in the request body.

Business rules: Users must select a reason category from predefined violation types. The optional report_details field allows detailed explanation to support the claim. The system enforces rate limiting to prevent report abuse and may prevent duplicate reports from the same user for the same review.

Validation: The report_reason field must match one of the platform's valid violation categories (spam, offensive_language, fake_review, not_about_product, personal_information, other). The report_details field, when provided, is limited to 1000 characters and should provide meaningful context for moderators.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the moderation log entry.

This UUID serves as the primary key for the moderation log record in the shopping_mall_review_moderation_logs table and uniquely identifies each administrative action taken on a product review.

Generated automatically when a moderation action is recorded and remains immutable throughout the log entry's lifecycle.

shopping_mall_review_id.description:
Foreign key reference to the product review that was moderated.

This field establishes the relationship between the moderation log entry and the specific review that was subject to administrative action, referencing the shopping_mall_reviews.id column.

Multiple moderation log entries can reference the same review over time as it progresses through different moderation states and administrative actions.

Links to the shopping_mall_admins.id column to identify which platform administrator executed this moderation decision. This field is critical for accountability, audit trails, and tracking individual moderator performance and decision patterns.

This field is nullable to support automated system actions that occur without direct administrator intervention, such as auto_approved or auto_flagged actions triggered by the platform's automated content analysis systems. When null, the action was performed by automated moderation algorithms rather than a human administrator.

oneOf.description:
Type of moderation action performed on the review.

Specifies the administrative decision or automated system action taken:

- auto_approved: Review automatically approved by system validation without manual intervention
- auto_flagged: Review automatically flagged by content analysis for manual review
- manual_approved: Review manually approved by administrator after moderation review
- manual_rejected: Review manually rejected by administrator due to policy violations
- edited_by_admin: Review content manually modified by administrator to remove violations
- deleted_by_admin: Review deleted by administrator for severe policy violations
- deleted_by_buyer: Review deleted by the original buyer who submitted it
- restored: Previously rejected or deleted review restored to active status

These action types align with the Prisma schema's action_type column and enable comprehensive audit trail tracking.

IShoppingMallReviewModerationLog.description:
Complete moderation log record tracking administrative actions on product reviews.

Represents a single entry in the review moderation audit trail from the shopping_mall_review_moderation_logs table, documenting all administrative and automated actions taken on product reviews including approvals, rejections, content edits, deletions, and reinstatements.

Each log entry captures the moderator's identity, the specific action taken, the detailed reasoning behind the decision, the before/after status of the review, and any automated system flags that triggered the action. This comprehensive audit trail provides complete transparency and accountability for the moderation process.

The moderation logs enable administrators to review the full history of moderation decisions, investigate specific incidents, ensure policy compliance, maintain quality standards for platform content, and improve moderation practices over time. These logs serve as the authoritative record for all interventions on user-generated review content.

Security: Access to moderation logs is restricted to platform administrators only, as these records contain sensitive internal decision-making information, policy enforcement details, and may reference user reports or legal considerations.

IShoppingMallReviewModerationLog.ISummar.description:
Summary representation of a review moderation action for list views and audit trails.

Provides lightweight information about administrative and automated actions taken on product reviews from the shopping_mall_review_moderation_logs table. Used in moderation history displays, audit logs, and administrative dashboards where complete action details are not required.

This summary variant focuses on essential moderation metadata including action type, status transitions, moderator identity, timestamps, and automated system flags, while excluding detailed justifications and internal notes to optimize performance in list contexts.

Maintains accountability and traceability through moderator references and complete status transition information, enabling administrators to track moderation patterns and identify records requiring detailed investigation.

page.description:
Page number for pagination, starting from 1.

Specifies which page of moderation log results to retrieve when working with large audit trails.

limit.description:
Number of moderation log entries to return per page.

Controls the page size for pagination, with a maximum limit of 100 entries to ensure reasonable response sizes and performance.

shopping_mall_admin_id.description:
Filter moderation logs by the administrator who performed the action.

When specified, returns only moderation actions performed by the specific administrator. Useful for reviewing an individual moderator's activity, performance evaluation, or investigating specific administrative decisions. Null or omitted returns logs from all moderators.

action_type.description:
Filter moderation logs by the type of action performed.

When specified, returns only logs matching the specified action type. Enables focused analysis of specific moderation activities. The valid action types are:
- auto_approved: Review automatically approved by system
- auto_flagged: Review automatically flagged by content filters
- manual_approved: Review manually approved by administrator
- manual_rejected: Review manually rejected by administrator
- edited_by_admin: Review content edited by administrator
- deleted_by_admin: Review deleted by administrator
- deleted_by_buyer: Review deleted by the buyer who created it
- restored: Previously deleted or rejected review restored to visibility

Null or omitted returns logs for all action types.

previous_status.description:
Filter moderation logs by the review status before the moderation action was applied.

When specified, returns only logs where the review had the specified status prior to the moderation action (pending_moderation, approved, rejected). Useful for analyzing status transitions, such as finding all reviews that were approved but later rejected, or tracking reviews that moved from pending to approved. Null or omitted returns logs for all previous statuses.

new_status.description:
Filter moderation logs by the resulting review status after the action.

When specified, returns only logs where the moderation action resulted in the specified status (pending_moderation, approved, rejected). Useful for analyzing outcomes of moderation decisions and status transitions. Null or omitted returns logs for all resulting statuses.

moderation_reason.description:
Filter moderation logs by searching within the moderation reasoning text.

When specified, performs a partial text match against the moderation_reason field to find logs containing specific justifications, policy violation details, or administrative notes. Useful for investigating patterns in specific types of rejections, tracking enforcement of particular policies, or searching for logs related to specific compliance issues.

Supports partial matching to enable flexible searches across the reasoning text (maximum 1000 characters as per Prisma schema). For example, searching for "profanity" would find all logs where profanity was cited as a reason. Null or omitted returns logs regardless of moderation reasoning content.

from.description:
Filter moderation logs to include only actions performed on or after this timestamp.

Enables date range filtering by specifying the start of the time window. Useful for analyzing moderation activity within specific periods or investigating recent moderation decisions. Null or omitted includes logs from the beginning of time.

to.description:
Filter moderation logs to include only actions performed on or before this timestamp.

Enables date range filtering by specifying the end of the time window. Used in combination with 'from' parameter to define precise time ranges for moderation activity analysis. Null or omitted includes logs up to the current time.

sort_by.description:
Field to sort the moderation log results by.

Specifies the ordering criterion for the returned logs:
- created_at: Sort by timestamp of the moderation action (default)
- action_type: Sort alphabetically by action type

Null or omitted defaults to sorting by created_at in descending order (most recent first).

order.description:
Sort order direction for the results.

Specifies whether to sort in ascending (asc) or descending (desc) order based on the sort_by field. Null or omitted defaults to descending order to show most recent moderation actions first.

IShoppingMallReviewModerationLog.IReques.description:
Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering review moderation logs.

Provides comprehensive filtering capabilities for retrieving moderation audit trails with support for pagination, moderator filtering, action type filtering, previous and new status filtering, moderation reason text search, date range filtering, and flexible sorting options. All filter parameters are optional, enabling both broad searches across all moderation activity and highly targeted queries for specific investigations.

This request structure enables administrators to efficiently analyze moderation patterns, investigate specific incidents, audit individual moderator performance, track policy compliance, search for specific policy violations or rejection reasons, track status transitions, and generate reports on moderation activities within defined time periods or matching specific criteria.
